present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the integral identity is elementary and settled.

title: The differential five-term relation needs related arguments
notes: The page writes \(\sum_{j=1}^5[\log u_j/(1-u_j)+\log(1-u_j)/u_j]du_j=0\), without relations among the five arguments.
statement: Set \(L(u)=\operatorname{Li}_2(u)+\tfrac12\log u\log(1-u)\). For \(0<x,y<1\), the five arguments \(x,y,(1-x)/(1-xy),1-xy,(1-y)/(1-xy)\) obey \(\sum L(u_j)=3L(1)=\pi^2/2\). Differentiating gives exactly the displayed one-form identity, since its summand is \(-2dL(u_j)\). It is false for five independently varying arguments.
reconstruction: The two-parameter substitution, range and branches are supplied; they cannot be recovered uniquely from the written equation alone.
fate: \citet[Chapter II, \S1.A, Rogers-dilogarithm five-term identity]{zagier2007dilogarithm} gives this precise classical identity.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected Rogers identity is established; the omitted relations are a source limitation.

title: Dilogarithms in algebraic K-theory
notes: The first entry is K-theory, with Bloch and Beilinson named.
statement: The following contribution supplies a concrete instance: a dilogarithmic primitive proves the Steinberg relation for the real regulator of \(K_2\) of a complex curve. This makes one precise connection, without interpreting the list as a theorem about every K-group.
reconstruction: The mathematical example is supplied from the immediately following talk; the introductory phrase has no independent quantifiers.
fate: \citet[\S1, Lemma 1 and the paragraph after it]{beilinson1980regulators} identifies the complex regulator and its real part, referring explicitly to Bloch's 1978 Irvine lectures. The lecture's precise construction is catalogued separately in record 476.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this connection is well established; the bare list does not identify a further theorem or open problem.

title: Combinatorial characteristic classes: the Gelfand--Gabrielov--Losik lead
notes: The second entry names combinatorial characteristic classes and the initials G.-G.-L.
statement: For a smooth manifold with a linearizable decomposition into simple cells satisfying the configuration-space connectivity condition (A), the Gelfand--Gabrielov--Losik construction produces a rational codimension-four cycle Poincar\'e dual to the first Pontryagin class. A real dilogarithmic variant enters this combinatorial construction. The notebook does not specify its normalization or a formula for a higher characteristic class.
reconstruction: This is a literature-supported identification of the named connection, with the original theorem's hypotheses retained. The source does not record enough to choose the dilogarithm's normalization or infer a new general characteristic-class claim.
fate: The precise cycle theorem is \citet[\S1, Proposition 10 and Theorem 1, Russian p.~18]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975computation}, published in 1975; receipt on 2 December 1974 is not a verified public circulation date. The later local formulation is \citet[Theorems 1--3]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1976local}. \citet[\S3, pp.~115--116]{goncharov1993classical} explicitly identifies the dilogarithmic ingredient in the 1975 construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the named connection is established and predates the talk; no additional conjecture is recoverable from the list.

title: Hyperbolic tetrahedral volume
notes: The third entry mentions the volume of a non-Euclidean tetrahedron and Gauss.
statement: For an oriented ideal hyperbolic tetrahedron whose vertices on the sphere at infinity have cross-ratio \(z\), its signed volume is \(D(z)=\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(z)+\log|z|\arg(1-z)\). Orientation reversal changes the sign. A general finite tetrahedron needs a more elaborate formula.
reconstruction: Ideal vertices, orientation and cross-ratio are additional specifications. The source's unqualified tetrahedron is not silently identified with this special case.
fate: \citet[Chapter I, \S4, eq.~(4.1)]{zagier2007dilogarithm} states the ideal-tetrahedron formula and its classical historical setting. This is a precise special case of the notebook's broad reference; no priority claim for Gauss alone is inferred.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the ideal-volume identity is established; this page does not select a general tetrahedral-volume formula.

title: Apéry's zeta(3) result and an unspecified dilogarithm link
notes: The fourth entry is simply \(\zeta(3)\), with Apéry's name.
statement: Apéry's theorem asserts \(\zeta(3)\notin\mathbb Q\). The notebook gives no integral, recurrence, special-value identity or reduction of that theorem to a dilogarithm; those are not reconstructed as an additional claim.
reconstruction: The established theorem and the unidentified link are deliberately separated.
fate: \citet[pp.~11--13]{apery1979irrationalite} is the primary 1979 publication from the 1978 arithmetic meeting. It confirms the irrationality result but does not identify the particular dilogarithmic connection intended by this list.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, Apéry's irrationality theorem is settled; the content of the listed connection is not sufficiently specified to classify as an open problem.

title: Web geometry and Bol
notes: The fifth entry names webs and Bol, with no formula or web specified.
statement: The classical Bol five-web is the germ, at a generic point of \(\mathbb C^2\), of the foliations with first integrals \(x,y,x/y,(1-y)/(1-x),x(1-y)/(y(1-x))\). It has six independent Abelian relations, the maximal rank for a planar five-web, and is not locally equivalent to an algebraic web. The additional relation beyond those generated by three-subwebs is the dilogarithmic five-term identity.
reconstruction: The particular web and its generic-point hypothesis come from the checked literature. This is a strong identification of the named example, not evidence that all of its hypotheses or rank claims were spoken in the seminar.
fate: \citet[\S6.1.4, p.~190; introduction p.~6]{pereirapirio2009web} states the foliations and relation and gives the nonalgebraizability argument; its bibliography attributes the example to Bol's 1936 paper. The original 1936 proof was not separately recovered. This explicit older result identifies the named connection, without converting the notebook list into a classification problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, Bol's exceptional web is established; the entry records no definite new open question.

title: Scattering theory: an unqualified connection
notes: A sixth entry in the right margin reads scattering theory.
statement: No scattering equation, dimension, observable, loop order or dilogarithmic identity is stated. Consequently the remark has no determinate mathematical proposition beyond suggesting an area of application.
fate: Primary-source searches combining dilogarithms with scattering and amplitudes yield many inequivalent applications. None can be designated the fate of this particular remark without a model or formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the intended application remains unidentified; no open scattering problem is manufactured from the label.

title: The zeta(2) integral has a missing minus sign
notes: Equation (3) states \(\int_0^1\log x\,dx/(1-x)=\sum 1/n^2\), with no visible minus sign in the scan.
statement: The correct identity is \(\int_0^1\log x\,dx/(1-x)=-\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-2}=-\pi^2/6\). Expanding \((1-x)^{-1}\) and applying monotone convergence to the nonnegative function \(-\log x/(1-x)\) justifies termwise integration.
reconstruction: The lower limit on the sum and the minus sign are supplied; the elementary justification is editorial.
fate: This is a classical dilogarithm evaluation; compare \citet[Chapter I, \S1]{zagier2007dilogarithm}. Its sign is also forced by the negative integrand on \((0,1)\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected identity is settled; both transcriptions faithfully retain the notebook's sign error.

title: Bloch's proposed replacement of zeta(2) by a curve zeta function
notes: The introduction says generalization to curves, names Bloch, and replaces the right-hand zeta value by the curve's zeta function.
statement: No base number field, arithmetic model, value of the complex parameter, order of vanishing, regulator determinant or rational factor is recorded. There is therefore no uniquely recoverable special-value formula or conjecture.
fate: \citet[\S1 and bibliography item 1]{beilinson1980regulators} explicitly relates the real regulator to Bloch's 1978 Irvine lectures. Its later \S2 concerns higher regulators and L-values, but that is not evidence that all those conjectural quantifiers were stated here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the historical regulator context is identifiable; the vague zeta remark remains unsuitable for an independent problem record.

title: A closed real regulator one-form
notes: For nowhere-zero holomorphic functions on a Riemann surface the notes define \(\omega_{f,g}=\log|f|d\arg g-\log|g|d\arg f\) and infer that integration along paths is well defined.
statement: On a Riemann surface where \(f,g\) are holomorphic units, \(d\arg f=\operatorname{Im}(df/f)\) is globally defined and \(d\omega_{f,g}=0\). Hence its integrals depend only on the relative homology class of a path with fixed endpoints; closedness does not assert independence of every path between those endpoints.
reconstruction: The global one-form is distinguished from a globally chosen argument function; path homotopy or homology is the required qualification.
fate: The real regulator is attributed to Bloch's 1978 lectures in \citet[\S1, paragraph following Lemma 1]{beilinson1980regulators}. The displayed differential identity also follows directly from the Cauchy--Riemann equations.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the closed-form construction is established; nonzero periods are precisely part of its regulator content.

title: Bilinearity and alternation of the real regulator form
notes: Equations (6)--(7) give additivity in a product of functions and antisymmetry under interchanging them.
statement: For holomorphic units, \(\omega_{f_1f_2,g}=\omega_{f_1,g}+\omega_{f_2,g}\), \(\omega_{f,g_1g_2}=\omega_{f,g_1}+\omega_{f,g_2}\), and \(\omega_{g,f}=-\omega_{f,g}\). These are equalities of differential forms, not merely of cohomology classes.
fate: These elementary identities underlie Bloch's real regulator, recalled by \citet[\S1]{beilinson1980regulators}; they are already implicit in the logarithmic formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the identities are exact on the common domain of invertibility.

title: The single-valued dilogarithm proves the Steinberg relation
notes: The form \(\omega_{f,1-f}\) is asserted to be exact. Equation (9) writes its primitive using a logarithm term and the imaginary part of an integral, and emphasizes single-valuedness.
statement: The Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm \(D(z)=\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(z)+\log|z|\arg(1-z)\) is single valued on \(\mathbb C\setminus\{0,1\}\), extends continuously by zero at \(0,1,\infty\), and satisfies \(dD(z)=\log|z|d\arg(1-z)-\log|1-z|d\arg z\). Consequently \(\omega_{f,1-f}=d(D\circ f)\) whenever \(f,1-f\) are holomorphic units.
reconstruction: Individual logarithms and the complex dilogarithm require local branches; their stated combination is the global function. The lower endpoint zero is understood by its continuous limit.
fate: \citet[Chapter I, \S3]{zagier2007dilogarithm} records the precise single-valued function and differential. The pre-1979 Bloch regulator context is confirmed in \citet[\S1]{beilinson1980regulators}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this exactness identity and hence the real Steinberg relation are established.

title: David Wigner and continuous cohomology of SL(2)
notes: The notebook attributes the single-valued function to D. Wigner and says he connected it to continuous cohomology of \(SL(2)\).
statement:
Fix \(x\in\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\). For generic quadruples, put
\[
c_x(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)
=D\bigl(\operatorname{cr}(g_0x,g_1x,g_2x,g_3x)\bigr).
\]
The five-term identity makes this a homogeneous measurable real three-cocycle for \(GL_2(\mathbb C)\), restricting to \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\). It represents the nonzero degree-three volume class under the comparison between measurable and continuous cohomology. Changing \(x\) gives a cohomologous cocycle.
reconstruction: The complex group, real coefficients, degree, generic quadruples and comparison map are supplied from the literature. This identifies a standard precise version of the note; the notebook itself suppresses these data.
fate: \citet[\S3, p.~117, eqs.~(10)--(12)]{goncharov1993classical} explicitly attributes this construction to Wigner and places it in the 1970s. The 1993 chapter is the checked exposition, not the first-circulation date of Wigner's observation; no original Wigner preprint date was verified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the volume-cocycle interpretation is established; the source's omission of field and degree is recorded rather than treated as an open problem.

title: A puncture period and the tame symbol
notes: Equation (10) equates a small-loop integral of \(\omega_{f,g}\) with \(\log|f^{v_x(g)}/g^{v_x(f)}|(x)\), without a factor \(2\pi\).
statement: Let \(f=z^m a(z)\), \(g=z^n b(z)\) near \(x\), with \(a(0)b(0)\ne0\). For a positively oriented small circle \(\gamma_x\), \(\int_{\gamma_x}\omega_{f,g}=2\pi\log|a(0)^n/b(0)^m|=2\pi\log|\partial_x\{f,g\}|\), where \(\partial_x\{f,g\}=(-1)^{mn}a(0)^n/b(0)^m\).
reconstruction: Orientation, local expansions and the tame sign are specified. The tame sign disappears under absolute value but not in the later complex symbol.
fate: The complex local tame-symbol identity is \citet[\S1, Lemma 1(b)]{beilinson1980regulators}; taking logarithmic absolute values gives the corrected real normalization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected period identity is exact. The missing factor is a faithful notebook error, not a translation issue.

title: Symbols present K2 of the function field, not automatically of the curve
notes: The notes quotient symbols by bimultiplicativity, antisymmetry and the Steinberg relation, then call the result both \(K_2(X)\) and K2 of its rational function field.
statement: For a field \(F\), Matsumoto's theorem identifies Quillen \(K_2(F)\) with the abelian group on \(\{f,g\}\), \(f,g\in F^\times\), subject to bimultiplicativity and \(\{f,1-f\}=0\) for \(f\ne0,1\). Skew symmetry follows from these relations. Taking \(F=\mathbb C(X)\) defines the function-field group; it does not by itself define \(K_2(X)\).
reconstruction: The ambient free group is made abelian, and the curve and function-field notation are separated.
fate: The result dates to Matsumoto's 1969 theorem, stated precisely in \citet[III.6.1]{weibel2013kbook}. The notebook's Milnor/Steinberg attribution is compatible with this older framework.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the field presentation is established; the missing passage to the curve is supplied by localization in the following item.

title: The unique smooth projective completion of an algebraic curve
notes: A parenthesis says an algebraic curve is compactified uniquely, for example by embedding it in projective space and taking the closure.
statement: A smooth connected algebraic curve over \(\mathbb C\) has a smooth projective completion unique up to the unique isomorphism extending the given open curve. The normalization of a projective closure gives that smooth completion. A raw projective closure can be singular; arbitrary open Riemann surfaces need not be algebraic or of finite type.
reconstruction: Smoothness, algebraicity, normalization and uniqueness relative to the given open immersion are the missing hypotheses. The preceding general Riemann surface is not silently assumed algebraic.
fate: This is the classical smooth-curve model used in the regulator construction of \citet[\S1]{beilinson1980regulators}; it is not a new theorem announced by this talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected completion statement is standard; the unrestricted topological or analytic reading is false.

title: Localization and extension of the real regulator over punctures
notes: Equation (12) writes \(K_2(X)\to K_2(\mathbb C(X))\to\bigoplus_x\mathbb C^*\). A sum of symbols with trivial local terms then gives a class in \(H^1(X,\mathbb R)\).
statement: For a smooth algebraic curve, localization identifies the image of \(K_2(X)\to K_2(\mathbb C(X))\) with the kernel of the sum of tame symbols. If \(\xi=\sum_i n_i\{f_i,g_i\}\) has trivial tame symbol at every point of \(X\), the closed form \(\sum_i n_i\omega_{f_i,g_i}\), initially off its divisors, has zero small-loop periods and determines a unique class in \(H^1(X,\mathbb R)\). This defines the real regulator on \(K_2(X)\) by composition.
reconstruction: The statement concerns an image/kernel exactness assertion. The notes do not supply a proof of injectivity of the first arrow, and no such assertion is needed for the regulator construction. Uniqueness is uniqueness of the extended cohomology class, not of an arbitrary differential form.
fate: \citet[\S1, immediately after Lemma 1]{beilinson1980regulators} explicitly uses Quillen's localization theorem and identifies the resulting logarithmic absolute value with Bloch's regulator, already circulated in his 1978 lectures.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular-curve regulator construction is established; it makes no special-value conjecture without further arithmetic data.

title: Beilinson's complex multiplicative regulator
notes: Equation (16) defines an exponentiated logarithmic integral in cases according to the winding number of \(g\), with a sign \((-1)^{v_\gamma(f)v_\gamma(g)}\). The symbol is said to be bimultiplicative, symmetric and Steinberg, and to recover the real construction.
statement: For a loop \(\gamma\) based at \(a\), avoid the divisors and continue chosen logarithms along the loop. A convenient equivalent formula is \[r_\gamma(f,g)=\exp\!\left[\frac{1}{2\pi i}\left(\int_\gamma\log f\,d\log g-\log g(a)\int_\gamma d\log f\right)\right].\] It is independent of the initial logarithm choices, homotopy invariant, bimultiplicative, multiplicatively skew, and satisfies \(r_\gamma(f,1-f)=1\). On a puncture circle it is the tame symbol. Moreover \(\log|r_\gamma(f,g)|=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_\gamma\omega_{f,g}\), so unramified symbols yield the complex refinement of the real regulator.
reconstruction: The basepoint formula makes branch normalization explicit and avoids the notebook's case division. Multiplicative skew symmetry means \(r_\gamma(g,f)=r_\gamma(f,g)^{-1}\); literal symmetry would generally be false. Taking logarithmic absolute value, with the stated factor, is the recovery of the real regulator.
fate: This is an exact construction match to \citet[\S1, eq.~(1) and Lemma 1]{beilinson1980regulators}, published in 1980. The journal records receipt on 21 December 1979; no earlier public preprint date was verified. The notebook documents the seminar on 19 November 1979. The paper also acknowledges an independent unpublished construction by Deligne.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this regulator refinement was published soon after the seminar and is established. It is not merely a retrospective thematic link to later Beilinson conjectures.

title: Stable Steinberg extension and second group homology
notes: For an affine curve the notes write \(K_2(X)=H_2(SL_n(A),\mathbb Z)\) and \(1\to K_2(X)\to St^X\to SL^X\to1\), where \(A\) is its ring of algebraic functions.
statement: For a unital ring \(A\), the stable Steinberg group gives the universal central extension \(1\to K_2(A)\to\operatorname{St}(A)\to E(A)\to1\), and \(K_2(A)\cong H_2(E(A),\mathbb Z)\). If \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\), its algebraic K2 is \(K_2(A)\). Replacing the stable elementary group by a particular \(SL_n(A)\) requires both the relevant equality with the elementary group and homology/K2 stability hypotheses.
reconstruction: The stable rank and elementary-group qualifications are essential. They are supplied rather than choosing an unjustified finite rank for the source.
fate: The Kervaire--Steinberg theorem is stated in \citet[III.5.5; stability discussion III.5.5.2]{weibel2013kbook}, which traces the older Milnor/Steinberg theory. It does not assert the displayed equality for arbitrary \(n\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the stable statement is established; the source's unspecified finite-rank formulation is not a complete theorem.

title: Promoting Lagrange multipliers to canonical variables
notes: The multiplier \(\lambda\) is paired with a momentum \(\pi\), and the extended constraints are \(G_a=(\pi_\mu,T_\mu)\). Gauge conditions include \(-\dot\lambda^\mu+\chi^\mu\). The count is \((n+m)-2m=n-m\).
statement: For a regular irreducible bosonic system with \(n\) canonical pairs and \(m\) independent first-class constraints, add \(m\) multiplier pairs. The extended phase space has dimension \(2(n+m)\), and its \(2m\) first-class constraints, when regularly reduced, leave dimension \(2(n-m)\). Differential gauge conditions for the multipliers can be encoded by a suitable extended Hamiltonian. This is a local degree-of-freedom count, not a proof that arbitrary gauges are admissible.
reconstruction: The count refers to independent regular bosonic constraints. The overwritten sign and momentum index in source equation (4) are not silently repaired; the clear equations (6)--(7) determine the construction.
fate: The contemporaneous publication leads are \citet[pp.~309--312]{batalinvilkovisky1977relativistic} and \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}. The later Hamiltonian framework is explicitly described in \citet[introduction and \S~II]{bering1997geometry}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular extended-phase-space construction is established; the literal ambiguous formula (4) remains a transcription uncertainty.

title: Ghost canonical pairs and the BFV phase-space action
notes: Equation (8) integrates \((q^A,p_A,\eta^a,\mathcal P_a)\) with phase \(\int(p_A\dot q^A+\mathcal P_a\dot\eta^a-H_{\rm complete})dt\).
statement: For each constraint \(G_a\), introduce a ghost \(\eta^a\) of opposite parity and its conjugate momentum \(\mathcal P_a\), with ghost numbers \(+1\) and \(-1\). The full symplectic structure is even. With a chosen time-slicing, boundary states and integration prescription the displayed phase-space expression is the formal BFV partition functional.
reconstruction: Ghost number, parity and boundary prescriptions are supplied. Odd ghost variables do not make the ambient Poisson bracket odd, and no BV antifields have been introduced.
fate: The boson/fermion extension belongs to the 1977/1978 Hamiltonian publications just cited. \citet[\S~II and \S~V.2, eq.~(V.8)]{bering1997geometry} writes the later precise geometric version and states its assumptions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is the standard Hamiltonian ghost extension; the displayed continuum integral remains formal without further analytic construction.

title: Nilpotent Hamiltonian charge, invariant Hamiltonian and gauge fermion
notes: Equations (9)--(11) require \(\{\Omega,\Omega\}=0\), \(\{H_1,\Omega\}=0\), and \(H_{\rm complete}=H_1-\{\Psi,\Omega\}\), with \(\Psi=\mathcal P_a\chi^a\).
statement: Let the odd charge \(\Omega\) have ghost number one and satisfy the even-bracket master equation \(\{\Omega,\Omega\}=0\). Let \(H_1\) be even, ghost number zero, and BRST invariant. For any admissible odd gauge fermion \(\Psi\) of ghost number minus one, the displayed gauge-fixed Hamiltonian is again BRST invariant by the graded Jacobi identity.
reconstruction: Parities and ghost numbers make the equations precise; the sign of the gauge-fixing term is conventional once \(\Psi\) is fixed.
fate: \citet[\S~II, eq.~(II.6), and \S~V.2]{bering1997geometry} gives this Hamiltonian structure and attributes it to the earlier BFV work. The original 1977/1978 articles are indirect publication checks, not a claim that the 1979 notes anticipated the later Lagrangian BV formalism.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the algebraic BRST-invariance statement is exact; admissibility and quantum gauge independence require the additional hypotheses in item 1979-478.7.

title: Solving the Hamiltonian BRST equations as a formal series
notes: The speaker says the equations for \(\Omega\) and \(H_1\) can be solved as series in ghosts and ghost momenta whenever the constraints are first class.
statement: For a regular irreducible first-class constraint system, with the usual acyclic constraint resolution locally, one can recursively construct a formal charge beginning \(\Omega=\eta^aG_a+\cdots\) and a BRST extension of a Hamiltonian preserving the constraints. Reducible systems need further ghosts; singular constraints need additional hypotheses. Formal solvability asserts neither convergence nor finite termination.
reconstruction: Regularity, irreducibility or a suitable resolution, locality and formality are necessary additions to the notebook's all-first-class wording.
fate: \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization} is the contemporaneous graded-constraint publication lead. \citet[introduction]{bering1997geometry} confirms the later BFV framework but assumes, rather than proves, the existence of the charge used in that article. The original recursive proof was not recovered here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular formal existence framework is established; an unrestricted singular-system theorem is not verified by the notes or the checked publication text.

title: Termination of the supergravity ghost expansion
notes: The series are said usually to terminate in supergravity.
statement: A finite ghost-degree bound depends on the particular supergravity theory, formulation, auxiliary fields and constraint generators. None is specified, so the word usually does not define a universal termination theorem.
fate: The contemporary modified-rule lead is \citet[pp.~141--152]{kallosh1978modified}. The later open-algebra discussion in \citet[\S2.2]{fuster2005brst} confirms the relevant phenomenon but supplies no model-independent bound matching this phrase.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, model-specific constructions exist; this notebook remark remains too imprecise for a separate open-problem identifier.

title: Hamiltonian BRST transformations and nilpotence
notes: Equation (12) writes \(\delta X=\{X,\Omega\}\mu\), with \(\mu\) an odd constant.
statement: The differential \(sX=\{X,\Omega\}\), with a consistent right/left derivation convention, has odd parity and satisfies \(s^2=0\) when \(\{\Omega,\Omega\}=0\). A constant odd parameter gives an even infinitesimal change of integration variables. The symplectic potential changes by an endpoint term, so invariance of an action also depends on boundary conditions.
reconstruction: Nilpotence is a property of the odd derivation itself, not merely a vacuous consequence of the square of one Grassmann parameter being zero.
fate: \citet[\S~II, eq.~(II.6), and \S~V.2, eq.~(V.9)]{bering1997geometry} displays the nilpotent charge and the endpoint condition in the Hamiltonian setting.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the algebraic identity is exact, with boundary conditions needed for the integrated action.

title: Field-dependent BRST change of variables and gauge independence
notes: The last formula chooses \(\mu=i\int\mathcal P_a\,\delta\chi^a\,dt\) and concludes BRST invariance.
statement: For an infinitesimal change of an admissible gauge fermion, a BRST change of path variables with a field-dependent odd parameter can compensate the change of gauge-fixing action through its Jacobian. This proves formal gauge independence only when the measure is BRST compatible, boundary terms vanish, the gauges are connected without a singularity, and no global orbit obstruction has been ignored.
reconstruction: A field-dependent parameter does not generate an ordinary canonical transformation with unit Jacobian. The Jacobian, rather than constant-parameter invariance alone, is the crucial missing step.
fate: \citet[\S~II, \S~V.2 and \S~V.3]{bering1997geometry} analyzes precisely this field-dependent path-space change and states explicitly that global Gribov problems, phase-space boundaries and existence of the path integral are excluded or assumed. Its arXiv preprint first circulated in September 1997; the mechanism itself is attributed there to the original BFV work.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the qualified formal BFV theorem is established; the notes do not prove a global, nonperturbative gauge-independence theorem.

title: First-generation charges and valence nucleon diagrams
notes: The diagrams pair \((\nu,e)\) and \((u,d)\), assign charges \((0,-1)\) and \((2/3,-1/3)\), and draw proton \(uud\) and neutron \(udd\).
statement: In units of the positron charge, the first-generation charge eigenvalues are \(Q(\nu_e)=0\), \(Q(e)=-1\), \(Q(u)=2/3\), \(Q(d)=-1/3\). The valence assignments give \(Q(uud)=1\) and \(Q(udd)=0\). The valence picture does not assert that a physical nucleon has only three constituents and no gluon or sea-quark degrees of freedom.
reconstruction: The scan's circles are interpreted as valence diagrams, and charge eigenvalues are distinguished from an identity matrix acting on a doublet.
fate: These are pre-1979 quark-model and electroweak assignments. Their current representation conventions are stated in \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak}; the QCD field content is given in \citet[\S9.1]{hustonrabbertzzanderighi2026qcd}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, these charge assignments remain standard; the schematic nucleon drawing is not a full wavefunction.

title: Three quark and lepton generations
notes:
The page lists \((
u_e,e),(
u_\mu,\mu),(
u_	au,	au)\) and \((u,d),(c,s),(t,b)\), marking the top quark as not yet found.
statement: The three-generation model repeats the same gauge-representation pattern for three families, while masses and mixing parameters differ. The table is a field-content proposal; it is not a derivation of the number three or of the masses. Heavy charged leptons and quarks decay, but the blanket wording that every later-generation particle quickly disappears does not describe neutrino propagation.
reconstruction: Historical non-observation is separated from present field content. Rounded handwritten masses are not used as current numerical data.
fate: \citet[pp.~654--657]{kobayashimaskawa1973cp} already studies six-quark weak mixing in 1973. The current three-generation CKM construction is \citet[\S12.1]{ceccucciligetisakai2026ckm}; neutrino propagation and mixing are described in \citet[\S14.1]{gonzalezgarciawendell2026neutrinos}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, all three generations form the established phenomenological framework, including the top quark; neutrino masses require extending the massless-neutrino model described in 1979.

title: Colour triplets, singlets and eight adjoint gluons
notes: Each quark is tripled into colour components, \(SU(3)_c\) acts by a unitary matrix, leptons are not tripled, and eight gluons are identified with the adjoint representation.
statement: Each quark flavour transforms in the fundamental \(\mathbf3\) of \(SU(3)_c\); leptons are colour singlets. The gauge connection takes values in \(\mathfrak{su}(3)\), whose dimension is eight, and its homogeneous colour rotation is adjoint. A local gauge transformation of the connection also has an inhomogeneous derivative term.
reconstruction: The ambiguous adjoint annotation on P000890 is attached to the gauge field as clarified on P000892; it is not used to place quarks in the eight-dimensional adjoint representation.
fate: \citet[\S9.1, eq.~(9.1) and its definitions]{hustonrabbertzzanderighi2026qcd} states the QCD representation and curvature conventions. This is confirmation of the older framework, not a later resolution of a seminar conjecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the representation distinction is established and unchanged.

title: Chiral weak doublets, singlets and hypercharge
notes: The weak group mixes each doublet synchronously and is written \(SU(2)\times U(1)\) on P000891, but \(SU(2)\times SU(1)\) on P000892. The right electron is called a singlet under the displayed product.
statement: With \(Q=T_3+Y\), the lepton representations are \(L_L=(\nu_L,e_L)\sim(\mathbf2,-1/2)\) and \(e_R\sim(\mathbf1,-1)\) under \(SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y\). The right electron is a singlet only of the \(SU(2)\) factor. Gauge transformations are continuous linear transformations, not merely permutations of particle labels. The minimal model has no right-handed neutrino field.
reconstruction: The Abelian group and nontrivial right-electron hypercharge are restored. Spontaneous symmetry breaking, rather than unequal masses by themselves, explains why the vacuum need not exhibit the whole weak symmetry.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons} gives the earlier chiral model; \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak} states modern normalizations.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected representation assignment is standard; a right-electron singlet of the entire product would have zero electric charge.

title: Dirac matrices, chirality and the massless limit
notes: The talk writes the Dirac equation, the Clifford anticommutator and chiral projectors. Its displayed \(\gamma^5\) has the opposite sign to one common convention, so the projector labeled left is \((1+\gamma^5)/2\).
statement: For \(\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}\) and \(\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)\), choose \(\gamma^5\) with \((\gamma^5)^2=1\) and \(\{\gamma^5,\gamma^\mu\}=0\). Then \(P_\pm=(1\pm\gamma^5)/2\) are complementary projectors. The massless Dirac equation separates into two Weyl equations; a mass term couples them. For positive-energy massless particles chirality matches helicity after fixing conventions, but for massive particles they are distinct notions.
reconstruction: The sign of \(\gamma^5\) is treated as a convention, not a transcription mistake. A four-component notation for a Weyl neutrino does not decide whether actual massive neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana.
fate: The chiral lepton construction is already used in \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons}. \citet[\S14.1]{gonzalezgarciawendell2026neutrinos} distinguishes the massless minimal model from the observed neutrino-mixing framework.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the Clifford and projection identities are exact; the notebook's massless-neutrino assumption is a historical model assumption.

title: Photon, charged-current and neutral-current exchange
notes: Feynman sketches show photon, \(W^-\) and \(Z^0\) exchange. The photon is massless, the weak bosons massive, and approximate mass predictions are labeled about \(85m_p\) and \(95m_p\).
statement: In the electroweak model a massless photon couples to the electromagnetic charge current, charged \(W^\pm\) bosons couple the two left-handed components of weak doublets, and a neutral \(Z\) couples to a weak neutral current. Gauge-boson lines in a perturbative diagram represent propagators carrying four-momentum. The 1979 masses are model predictions and rough numerical estimates, not measurements supplied by the source.
reconstruction: The diagram's particle labels are read as examples of the interaction vertices; no exact cross section or claim of experimental discovery in 1979 is inferred.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(5)--(14)]{weinberg1967leptons} derives the earlier mass and current structure. Current measured masses and electroweak fits are treated in \citet[\S10.4.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the weak gauge bosons are experimentally established; detailed current couplings and the tree-level mass relation are reconstructed in record 480.

title: Non-Abelian curvature and the gauge kinetic action
notes: Equations (8)--(11) define adjoint-indexed vector fields, curvature with a quadratic term, a trace normalization and the Yang--Mills kinetic Lagrangian. Both curvature factors are printed with upper spacetime indices.
statement:
For a connection \(A_\mu=A_\mu^aT_a\), define \(D_\mu=\partial_\mu+igA_\mu\) and \([D_\mu,D_
u]=igF_{\mu
u}\). Contract the curvature using an invariant Lie-algebra form and the spacetime metric: \(\mathcal L_{m YM}=-	frac14F^a_{\mu
u}F^{a\mu
u}\) in the standard normalization. Matrix traces depend on the representation: for conventionally normalized \(SU(N)\), \(\operatorname{tr}_{m fund}T_aT_b=	frac12\delta_{ab}\) but \(\operatorname{tr}_{m adj}T_aT_b=N\delta_{ab}\).
reconstruction: The metric contraction is restored. The notebook's adjoint trace value needs a stated rescaling of the invariant form, or a correction of the representation label; it is not a universal trace convention.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1)--(11)]{yangmills1954conservation} is the original non-Abelian construction; \citet[\S9.1]{hustonrabbertzzanderighi2026qcd} gives the current QCD normalization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the invariant curvature action is established; the compressed indices and trace convention require the stated corrections.

title: Minimal gauge coupling of fermions
notes: The matter term is \(\bar\Psi i\widehat D\Psi\), with \(D_\mu=\partial_\mu+igI^aA^a_\mu\) and \(\widehat D=\gamma^\mu D_\mu\). It is described as massless before adding scalar fields.
statement: The generators in \(D_\mu\Psi\) must act in the representation carried by \(\Psi\), which need not be the adjoint representation of the gauge field. With that choice, \(\bar\Psi i\gamma^\mu D_\mu\Psi\) is gauge invariant. A bare Dirac mass is gauge invariant only if the left- and right-handed representations can be paired; the chiral electroweak electron needs a Higgs Yukawa coupling instead.
reconstruction: The representation on matter is separated from the adjoint field index, avoiding the misleading implication that all matter generators are adjoint matrices.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons} is the relevant pre-existing chiral matter construction; \citet[eqs.~(1)--(6)]{yangmills1954conservation} gives the original covariant-derivative mechanism.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, minimal coupling is standard; the bare-mass prohibition depends on the representation, not solely on the presence of a gauge field.

title: Gauge-invariant Higgs potential and power counting
notes: A scalar multiplet and potential \(P(g\varphi)=P(\varphi)\) are added; the \(U(1)\) example is \(\lambda^2(\varphi_1^2+\varphi_2^2-\eta^2)^2\). The second power is called the maximum compatible with renormalizability.
statement: For a scalar of canonical mass dimension one in four spacetime dimensions, a polynomial interaction of degree at most four has a coupling of nonnegative mass dimension. Thus the displayed potential is quadratic in \(|\varphi|^2\) and quartic in the real scalar fields. Gauge invariance restricts it to invariant polynomials. Power counting is a necessary organizational criterion here, not by itself a proof of renormalizability for an arbitrary gauge model.
reconstruction: The spacetime dimension and the variable whose second power is meant are made explicit.
fate: \citet[eq.~(1)]{higgs1964broken} already uses this Abelian scalar-gauge model; \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons} gives the weak-doublet potential.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the quartic power-counting statement is established; no new renormalization theorem is present.

title: Classical vacuum as a minimum-energy configuration
notes: The last sentence identifies classical vacuum solutions with minimum energy and hence with minima of \(P(\varphi)\).
statement: In a trivial topological sector with compatible boundary conditions, canonical positive kinetic energy and potential bounded below, constant scalar configurations at global minima of \(P\), with vanishing field strength and covariant derivative, minimize the classical energy. Nontrivial boundary data, topological sectors or gauge constraints can obstruct that simple description. A local minimum is a metastable classical state, not automatically the global ground state.
reconstruction: The vanishing-gradient and boundary hypotheses needed to replace energy minimization by potential minimization are supplied.
fate: The symmetry-breaking vacuum choice is explicit in \citet[eqs.~(1)--(2)]{higgs1964broken} and \citet[eqs.~(3)--(5)]{weinberg1967leptons}. The following lecture develops the Hessian and mass spectrum around it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the qualified classical statement is standard; it makes no nonperturbative quantum-vacuum claim.

title: Coulomb interaction energy and divergent point-charge self-energies
notes: The two-source field-line drawing accompanies \(\int E^2dV\sim e^2/r\).
statement: For two static point charges in three spatial dimensions, subtracting the two separation-independent self-energies leaves an interaction \(V(r)=q_1q_2/(4\pi r)\) in rationalized units. The total \(\int|E|^2dV\) is divergent at the point charges unless they are regularized. Opposite charges have negative interaction energy even though the unsubtracted field-energy density is nonnegative.
reconstruction: The source's schematic proportionality is read as the separation-dependent energy after self-energy subtraction, not the literal divergent total integral.
fate: The Abelian Coulomb behavior is contrasted with area-law confinement in \citet[\S~II]{wilson1974confinement}, published 15 October 1974. The electrostatic scaling itself is much older.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the Coulomb comparison is established; the subtraction and charge-sign qualifications are essential.

title: A flux tube of distance-independent transverse size
notes: The page explicitly labels as a hypothesis that the tube cross-section or diameter does not depend on the separation of the sources.
statement: A fixed intrinsic core profile in a classical flux-tube model and the quantum mean-square transverse width of a fluctuating string are different observables. In the long-string effective theory at zero temperature, the latter has leading behavior \(w^2(r/2)=(d-2)(2\pi\sigma)^{-1}\log(r/r_0)\). Thus a strictly fixed quantum width is incompatible with that effective description even when the leading energy is \(\sigma r\).
reconstruction: The notebook specifies neither a width observable nor a classical/quantum averaging prescription. The effective-theory statement is a precise later comparison; it is not silently substituted for an exact theorem about the source's unspecified diameter.
fate: The later study \citet[eqs.~(1)--(3), with lattice comparison in Figs.~2--3]{gliozzipepewiese2010width} derives this broadening and tests it in \((2+1)\)-dimensional \(SU(2)\) lattice theory (preprint 26 February 2010; journal 2010). It cites the 1981 Lüscher--Münster--Weisz precursor. This is a developed correction of the naive picture, not a proof of the full four-dimensional continuum theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, distance-independent width is not a universal confinement criterion. Quantum broadening and finite intrinsic thickness can coexist, and neither alone settles the continuum static-potential problem.

title: Linear static energy and continuum confinement
notes: Constant cross-section and energy density are used to infer a string with \(\nu=d\varepsilon/d\ell\sim E^2\sigma\), where the source's \(\sigma\) denotes cross-sectional area.
statement: The elementary conditional inference is that constant energy per unit length gives \(V(r)=\tau r+O(1)\). A distinct sharp gauge-theory question is whether four-dimensional continuum pure \(SU(3)\) Yang--Mills theory at zero temperature has a positive asymptotic fundamental static string tension: \(\lim_{r\to\infty}V(r)/r=\tau>0\), where \(V(r)=-\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\log\langle W(r,T)\rangle\) after the appropriate static self-energy subtraction. Dynamical fundamental quarks are excluded from that asymptotic formulation.
reconstruction: The continuum, infinite-distance, zero-temperature and pure-gauge quantifiers are supplied to match the earlier problem 1975-377.10. The fixed-width hypothesis in item 1979-480.2 is stronger and is not part of that reused problem. The notation \(\tau\) avoids confusing tension with the source's area \(\sigma\).
fate: \citet[\S~IV, contrasted with \S~VI]{wilson1974confinement} establishes the lattice strong-coupling mechanism, not the continuum limit. \citet[\S4, eq.~(4.4) and Figs.~2--3]{bulava2019string} demonstrates string breaking in lattice QCD with light and strange dynamical quarks (preprint 11 February 2019; journal 2019). \citet[\S5]{jaffewitten2000yangmills} separates confinement from the existence-and-mass-gap problem; the latter remains officially unsolved in \citet[problem status]{clay2026yangmills}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the conditional tube-energy calculation is elementary; a complete rigorous four-dimensional continuum construction proving this asymptotic potential was not found in the checked literature. Lattice evidence and effective strings do not complete that theorem, and string breaking invalidates the same asymptotic assertion with dynamical quarks.
worth: A proof of a continuum positive string tension would be fundamental, but a bounded chapter calculation can only clarify the hypotheses and known controlled limits, not resolve confinement.

title: Manin's semiclassical qualification
notes: A remark attributed to Manin refers to quantizing Yang--Mills in a semiclassical approximation and says that no exact model yet exists.
statement: The recorded fragment gives no background solution, expansion parameter, observable or proposition about semiclassical asymptotics. It can qualify the preceding heuristic, but cannot be reconstructed as a definite semiclassical theorem or a separately quantified open problem.
reconstruction: No instanton, soliton or vacuum saddle is supplied merely because the word semiclassical occurs.
fate: The distinction between a formal or approximate gauge calculation and a construction of continuum quantum Yang--Mills theory is made explicit in \citet[\S\S2, 5--6]{jaffewitten2000yangmills}. This is context, not an exact publication match for Manin's unfinished sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the precise intended approximation remains unidentified; the broader construction problem is recorded separately.
speaker: Yu. I. Manin

title: The product gauge connection and electroweak kinetic terms
notes: The weak Lagrangian combines three \(SU(2)\) fields \(W^a\), an Abelian field \(B\), matter multiplets and a scalar multiplet; \(D_\mu=\partial_\mu+igt^aW^a_\mu+ig'yB_\mu\).
statement:
For \(SU(2)_L	imes U(1)_Y\), the connection has Lie-algebra components in \(\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak u(1)\). Its adjoint representation is a triplet plus a trivial one-dimensional factor. The gauge kinetic terms are \(-	frac14W^a_{\mu
u}W^{a\mu
u}-	frac14B_{\mu
u}B^{\mu
u}\); the Abelian curvature has no commutator term. Each matter covariant derivative uses that matter field's own representation and hypercharge.
reconstruction: The notebook's alternation between \(A\), \(W\) and \(H\) for fields or curvatures is disambiguated. A coupling omitted from a curvature can be absorbed by rescaling its connection; the choice must be consistent with the kinetic term.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons} gives the older model, and \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak} states the normalized modern Lagrangian.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the product-connection construction is established; its three-plus-one adjoint decomposition is not the representation of every fermion or scalar.

title: Scalar energy, stationary points and local vacua
notes: The scalar energy is \(T_{00}=\tfrac12\dot\varphi^2+\tfrac12|\nabla\varphi|^2+P(\varphi)\), called positive, and any local minimum of \(P\) is called a vacuum.
statement: With positive scalar kinetic form and a potential shifted so that its global minimum is zero, the classical energy density is nonnegative. In a trivial sector with compatible constant boundary data a constant global minimum minimizes the energy. A local minimum satisfies \(\nabla P=0\) and gives a candidate metastable state; stationary points alone need not be minima, and noncompact field space need not contain a global minimizer.
reconstruction: The energy shift, boundedness/existence assumptions and distinction between local and global minima are supplied. The word vacuum in the source is explicitly a local classical convention.
fate: The earlier scalar symmetry-breaking examples are \citet[eqs.~(1)--(2)]{higgs1964broken} and \citet[eqs.~(3)--(5)]{weinberg1967leptons}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the qualified energy argument is elementary; it does not establish a unique stable quantum vacuum.

title: Small oscillations and the scalar mass-squared Hessian
notes: Linearization at \(\lambda\) gives \(\Box\varphi^\alpha+P_{,\alpha\beta}(\lambda)\varphi^\beta=0\), but the subsequent plane-wave equation inserts an additional factor \(1/2\).
statement: For canonical kinetic term \(\tfrac12\partial_\mu\phi^\alpha\partial^\mu\phi^\alpha\) and \(\nabla P(\lambda)=0\), the mass-squared matrix is \(H_{\alpha\beta}=P_{,\alpha\beta}(\lambda)\). A plane wave obeys \(Hc=m^2c\), with no factor \(1/2\). The half in the Taylor expansion \(P(\lambda+\phi)=P(\lambda)+\tfrac12\phi^TH\phi+\cdots\) disappears when the equation is varied. A noncanonical kinetic metric would give a generalized eigenvalue problem instead.
reconstruction: The factor is corrected against both the scan and the Euler--Lagrange equation, not silently changed in the transcription.
fate: The scalar and vector fluctuation masses are already derived in \citet[eqs.~(2a)--(4)]{higgs1964broken}; the Hessian statement here also follows directly from the notebook's previous equation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected classical mass matrix is settled; the notebook's extra half is inconsistent with its canonical normalization.

title: Symmetry zero modes and the correct Goldstone count
notes: Differentiating \(P(g\varphi)=P(\varphi)\) gives zero modes \(I^a\lambda\). The text initially counts the generators but then observes that some vectors can be dependent.
statement: Let a compact Lie group \(G\) act orthogonally on a real scalar space, let \(P\) be invariant, and let \(\lambda\) be a stationary point. Differentiating the invariance identity gives \(H(T\lambda)=0\) for every \(T\in\mathfrak g\). Thus the Hessian kernel contains the tangent space of the orbit and has dimension at least \(r=\dim G-\dim G_\lambda\). Equality requires nondegeneracy transverse to the orbit; accidental flat directions can give additional zeros.
reconstruction: The rank of the orbit, rather than the dimension of the representation or all generators, is the exact symmetry count. Stationarity is used when the term containing \(\nabla P\) is dropped.
fate: The gauge-model relation to the older Goldstone result is discussed in \citet[opening paragraphs and eqs.~(2a)--(2c)]{higgs1964broken}. The finite-dimensional Hessian identity is explicitly derived in this notebook; it does not by itself prove the full quantum Goldstone theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the classical kernel statement is exact; the source's later dependence qualification repairs its initial overcount.

title: Unitary gauge, vector masses and conserved physical degrees of freedom
notes: A gauge is chosen to remove scalar components along Goldstone directions; the connection then acquires a quadratic mass term. The page counts \(2n\to3n\) vector polarizations and \(N\to N-n\) scalar components.
statement: Locally near a nonzero vacuum on a fixed orbit-type stratum, choose a slice transverse to the \(r\)-dimensional gauge orbit. The scalar kinetic term produces the positive semidefinite Gram mass matrix \((M^2)_{ab}=g_ag_b\langle T_a\lambda,T_b\lambda\rangle\), of rank \(r\). In four spacetime dimensions, \(r\) vector fields have three physical polarizations and \(n-r\) remain massless with two; \(N-r\) scalar components remain. The total count is \(2n+N=3r+2(n-r)+(N-r)\).
reconstruction: The source's \(3n\) count assumes every generator is broken. Unitary gauge is local and can fail at zeros of the scalar field or across different orbit strata; the claimed choice at every point is not a global theorem.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(2)--(4)]{higgs1964broken} gives the 1964 Abelian mechanism explicitly, including the new massive vector and remaining scalar; \citet[eqs.~(5)--(12)]{weinberg1967leptons} applies the partial breaking relevant here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the local classical Higgs mechanism is established; it redistributes physical polarizations without increasing their total number.

title: Exercise: eliminate the Goldstone field in the planar scalar model
notes: The explicit exercise asks to eliminate the Goldstone mode for \(P=\tfrac12(\varphi_1^2+\varphi_2^2-\eta^2)^2\), with \(G=O(2)\), and suggests shifting \(A\) by a derivative of an angle.
statement: On a patch with \(|\varphi|>0\), write \(\varphi=(\eta+h)(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\). For the connected \(SO(2)\) gauge action and convention \(D=\partial+gAJ\), set \(B_\mu=A_\mu+g^{-1}\partial_\mu\theta\). Then \(\tfrac12|D\varphi|^2=\tfrac12(\partial h)^2+\tfrac12g^2(\eta+h)^2B_\mu B^\mu\). The angular field disappears locally; the quadratic masses are \(m_B^2=g^2\eta^2\) and \(m_h^2=4\eta^2\) for the notebook's potential normalization.
reconstruction: The coupling convention, connected subgroup and nonvanishing-field patch are supplied. The disconnected reflection in \(O(2)\) supplies no additional infinitesimal Goldstone generator.
fate: This is the elementary local calculation underlying \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{higgs1964broken}, already published in 1964. The exercise is answered here as an annotation; it is not an unresolved problem or a new research result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the exercise has the displayed standard solution; a global angle is not asserted in sectors with zeros or winding.

title: The Higgs doublet and the unbroken electromagnetic subgroup
notes: The scalar is a two-component complex spinor with four real components. A gauge rotation puts it in \((0,\varphi_2)\), and one combination of \(t_3\) and hypercharge annihilates that vector. Three Goldstones are said to be eaten.
statement: Take a complex \(SU(2)\) doublet \(\Phi\) with \(Y=1/2\), and \(\langle\Phi\rangle=(0,v/\sqrt2)\). Then \(Q=T_3+Y\) annihilates the vacuum, leaving \(U(1)_{\rm em}\) unbroken. The orbit has dimension three: three of the four real scalar components supply longitudinal vector polarizations and one physical radial scalar remains. Spinor here describes the weak fundamental representation; the Higgs field is a Lorentz scalar.
reconstruction: The notebook's hypercharge symbol is rescaled and sign-changed on P000897; choosing \(Q=T_3+Y\) avoids treating that convention as a physical discrepancy. Gauging away three components is local near the chosen nonzero vacuum.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(3)--(12)]{weinberg1967leptons} is the direct pre-1979 model; \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak} fixes the current doublet normalization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this symmetry-breaking pattern and particle count are established; the remaining scalar's mass is a potential parameter, not fixed by the symmetry alone.

title: Diagonalizing the weak neutral mass matrix
notes: The displayed four-by-four matrix has charged entries \(a^2,a^2\) and neutral block \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^2&ab\\ab&b^2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with \(a\) proportional to \(g\) and \(b\) to \(g'\). It yields \(\tan\theta_w=g'/g\) and \(m_Z=m_W/\cos\theta_w\).
statement: The neutral block has determinant zero, eigenvalues \(0,a^2+b^2\), and orthogonal eigenvectors \((-b,a)\) and \((a,b)\). With the standard doublet normalization, \(m_W^2=g^2v^2/4\), \(m_Z^2=(g^2+g'^2)v^2/4\), and \(m_\gamma=0\), so \(m_W=m_Z\cos\theta_w\) at tree level. Changing the sign of the Abelian connection changes the off-diagonal sign but not the spectrum.
reconstruction: The vertical bars in equation (33) are read as delimiting the mass matrix, not merely as its determinant. The coupling relation requires the conventional hypercharge normalization and common vacuum scale.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(5)--(12)]{weinberg1967leptons} derives the direct earlier result. Radiative corrections and the distinction between mixing-angle schemes and measured masses are explicit in \citet[\S\S10.1--10.2]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the tree-level eigenvalue identity is exact; physical precision predictions include radiative corrections.

title: Charged, electromagnetic and neutral currents
notes: Equation (37) lists \(J^\pm,J^{\rm el},J^0\). Its neutral term has a prefactor read as \(q/\cos\theta_w\) and a single \(\sin\theta_w\) where the standard expression requires a square.
statement: For fixed generator and field conventions, \[\mathcal L_{\rm int}=-\frac{g}{\sqrt2}(J^-_\mu W^{+\mu}+J^+_\mu W^{-\mu})-eJ^{\rm em}_\mu A^\mu-\frac{g}{\cos\theta_w}(J^3_\mu-\sin^2\theta_w J^{\rm em}_\mu)Z^\mu,\quad e=g\sin\theta_w.\] Here \(J^3\) contains left-handed isospin and \(J^{\rm em}\) contains both chiralities with their electric charges. Vertex factors follow by differentiating the interaction action; probabilities further require amplitudes, sums over states and phase space.
reconstruction: The meanings of \(J^+\) and \(J^-\) are fixed with the chosen conjugate W fields. The neutral coupling and squared sine are emendations of the source; a charge operator cannot replace the universal weak prefactor.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(13)--(14)]{weinberg1967leptons} gives the earlier current structure; \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak} provides the modern normalization and chiral couplings.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected electroweak current formula is established; the original two coefficient errors would change neutral-current amplitudes.

title: Electron mass from a gauge-invariant Yukawa coupling
notes: The left lepton doublet and right electron are paired with the Higgs vacuum vector; after choosing \((0,\lambda)\) the term is \(f\lambda\bar e_Re_L+\mathrm{h.c.}\).
statement: With \(L_L\sim(\mathbf2,-1/2)\), \(e_R\sim(\mathbf1,-1)\), and \(\Phi\sim(\mathbf2,1/2)\), the invariant interaction is \(-y_e\bar L_L\Phi e_R+\mathrm{h.c.}\). At \(\Phi=(0,(v+h)/\sqrt2)\), it gives \(m_e=|y_e|v/\sqrt2\) after rephasing and the associated electron--Higgs coupling. The minimal field content leaves neutrinos massless; that is a limitation of this model, not an established property of actual neutrinos.
reconstruction: The scalar or conjugate scalar in the invariant contraction depends on whether the term is written with \(\bar L_L\) or \(\bar e_R\); the precise invariant expression fixes the source's suppressed conjugation.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1), (3)--(5)]{weinberg1967leptons} gives the earlier electron Yukawa term. The modern distinction between the minimal model and neutrino mass extensions is \citet[\S\S14.1--14.2]{gonzalezgarciawendell2026neutrinos}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the Yukawa mechanism is established, while neutrino masses and mixing require an extension of the massless minimal field content.

title: Quark Lagrangian and a unitary mixing matrix
notes: The final explicit question asks how to write the quark Lagrangian. Left-handed pairs use \((d',s',b')^T=V(d,s,b)^T\), and \(V\) is labeled orthogonal; right-handed quarks are singlets.
statement: For each generation, \(Q_L\sim(\mathbf3,\mathbf2,1/6)\), \(u_R\sim(\mathbf3,\mathbf1,2/3)\), \(d_R\sim(\mathbf3,\mathbf1,-1/3)\). Add gauge kinetic couplings and \(-\bar Q_LY_d\Phi d_R-\bar Q_LY_u\widetilde\Phi u_R+\mathrm{h.c.}\), where \(\widetilde\Phi=i\sigma_2\Phi^*\). Biunitary diagonalization of \(Y_u,Y_d\) gives \(V=U_{uL}^\dagger U_{dL}\) in charged currents. In the three-generation minimal model \(V\) is unitary and has three physical angles and one CP-violating phase; it is real orthogonal only after imposing a CP-conserving restriction.
reconstruction: The right-handed singlets refer only to weak \(SU(2)\); they still carry colour and hypercharge. The symbol resembling a superscript 1 on the down-type fields is interpreted through the clearly written primed mixing relation, not as a new generation label.
fate: \citet[pp.~654--657]{kobayashimaskawa1973cp} introduced the six-quark CP-violating structure before this talk. \citet[\S12.1, eqs.~(12.1)--(12.3)]{ceccucciligetisakai2026ckm} gives the explicit Yukawa and unitary-mixing construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the question has the standard displayed construction. The unrestricted orthogonality claim omits the physical CP phase and is not an open problem.

title: Gauge connections, ordered parallel transport and Wilson loops
notes: The notes write \(A_\mu=\sum_aT_aA_\mu^a\), \(\Psi(C)=\operatorname{Tr}P\exp\oint_C A\,dx\), and describe cancellation of an outward path followed by its reverse.
statement: For a smooth matrix connection and a piecewise smooth parametrized path \(\gamma\), parallel transport is the unique solution of the associated first-order matrix ODE, with prescribed initial identity. Reversing \(\gamma\) inverts transport, and concatenation multiplies transports in the chosen order. For a loop based at \(x\), gauge transformation conjugates \(U(C)\) by the gauge matrix at \(x\), so \(\operatorname{Tr}U(C)\) is gauge invariant.
reconstruction: The derivative \(dx\) in (3) is interpreted as \(dx^\mu\) contracted with \(A_\mu\). The side of matrix multiplication, sign of the connection, coupling and factors of \(i\) require a convention; the notes do not fix all of them.
fate: Wilson-loop gauge variables predate this talk: \citet[Secs.~II--III]{wilson1974confinement}; the corresponding loop notation is explicit in \citet[Sec.~4.1]{makeenko2000large}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A standard construction, with a fixed connection/transport sign convention. It is not by itself a construction of a continuum quantum measure.

title: Vanishing of gauge-variant expectations needs a precise observable
notes: \ru{Неинвар. величины в квант. теории получаются равными 0}: noninvariant quantities have zero quantum expectation.
statement: For a gauge-invariant finite-lattice measure without gauge fixing, the expectation of an observable equals that of its average over local gauge transformations. Hence an observable whose gauge average vanishes has zero expectation. A general noninvariant observable need not have zero expectation: it may contain a nonzero invariant component.
reconstruction: The gauge-average qualification is necessary. The notebook sentence is false if read as quantifying over every noninvariant function.
fate: \citet[abstract]{elitzur1975local} supplies the earlier local-gauge-symmetry result. Its publisher abstract was checked, not the full proof. The more elementary finite-volume projection statement here is an editorial consequence of invariance of the measure, so the publication match is recorded as partial.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected projection statement is established; gauge fixing changes the assertion about gauge-dependent quantities.

title: Gelfand on path-group characters and connections
notes: Gelfand says that a representation of the group of paths is determined by its character, and later calls such a representation a connection; curvature is compared with a Lie algebra.
statement: Finite-dimensional unitary representations of a group with identical characters are equivalent: restrict to the compact closure of their joint image and use compact-group character theory. A smooth connection determines a smooth transport functor on the thin path groupoid. Conversely, reconstructing a connection requires regularity and compatibility of transport, not merely an arbitrary algebraic representation of paths.
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional/unitary hypothesis and thin-path smoothness distinguish two claims compressed in the intervention. The curvature analogy is not a literal identification of curvature with a Lie algebra.
fate: Holonomy reconstruction is developed precisely in \citet[abstract]{barrett1991holonomy}. This later theorem clarifies the missing hypotheses; it is a partial match to Gelfand\textquotesingle s informal character argument, not evidence of a new 1980 theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established after specifying the category and regularity. The notes contain no unrestricted reconstruction theorem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Stokes-type loop functionals and the area derivative
notes: A small attached loop defines \(\delta\Psi/\delta\sigma_{\mu\nu}\); the notes explicitly warn that length is not a functional of this kind. Formula (7)/(10) inserts \(F_{\mu\nu}(x)\) inside the ordered trace.
statement: For smooth transport and an infinitesimal oriented rectangle at a marked point \(x\), the first term in its area is the curvature insertion: \(\delta W(C)/\delta\sigma^{\mu\nu}(x)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(F_{\mu\nu}(x)U(C_x))\), up to the agreed connection sign. A Stokes functional is insensitive to retracing and has an area derivative with this scaling; perimeter is not such a functional at a newly attached small loop.
reconstruction: Normalized \(W=N^{-1}\Psi\) is introduced for later consistency; the notes use unnormalized \(\Psi\). Orientation and the placement of the marked insertion must be fixed.
fate: The identity was already printed in \citet[Eq.~(12)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}, received 17 September and published 3 December 1979, with attribution to Mandelstam. The modern notation is \citet[Eq.~(147)]{makeenko2000large}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A classical differential identity, not a license to differentiate an unrenormalized quantum Wilson loop without a regulator.

title: Curvature from an infinitesimal commutator
notes:
Formula (13) writes a product of four factors \(1\pm dx_\mu
abla_\mu\) as \(1+dx_\mu\wedge dx_
u[
abla_\mu,
abla_
u]\); (11)--(14) implement shifts by differential operators.
statement:
For two smooth infinitesimal transport directions, \(e^{aD_\mu}e^{bD_
u}e^{-aD_\mu}e^{-bD_
u}=1+ab[D_\mu,D_
u]+O(|a|^2|b|+|a||b|^2)\). The mixed \(ab\) coefficient gives curvature. Replacing inverse exponentials by \(1-aD_\mu\) introduces unwanted pure quadratic terms unless only the mixed coefficient is retained.
reconstruction: Equation (13) must be read as a mixed infinitesimal identity, not as equality of finite products.
fate: This elementary small-rectangle calculation underlies the Mandelstam formula already used in \citet[Eq.~(12)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact} before the talk. The subsequent textbook presentation is \citet[Eq.~(147)]{makeenko2000large}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Valid as a mixed derivative or a properly truncated holonomy expansion. A literal finite-product identity is false.

title: Marked path derivatives become covariant derivatives
notes: Formulas (15)--(18) move the marked point, add a short connector and shift both ends of a closed transport; the notes emphasize that the left-hand derivative is noncommutative.
statement:
For a curvature-inserted loop \(\phi_{\mu
u}(C_x)=\operatorname{Tr}(F_{\mu
u}(x)U(C_x))\), the derivative defined by translating the insertion with short parallel-transport connectors is \(\partial^x_\alpha\phi_{\mu
u}=\operatorname{Tr}((D_\alpha F_{\mu
u})(x)U(C_x))\). Iteration gives covariant derivatives in the specified order. This operator is not an ordinary partial derivative on a scalar function of \(x\) alone.
reconstruction: We make explicit the connector-based definition that the notes state after using it. This resolves their warning about noncommutativity.
fate: The covariant derivative at the insertion is explicit in \citet[Eq.~(14) and the following explanation]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}, published December 1979; \citet[Eqs.~(148)--(150)]{makeenko2000large} gives the fuller path-derivative dictionary.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for classical smooth connections and suitable loop functionals.

title: Translation of a contour and the area-derivative integral
notes: Formula (19) decomposes whole-contour translation into endpoint derivatives and an integral of area derivatives; (20) specializes to translation-invariant closed-contour functionals.
statement: For an open-path Stokes functional with differentiable endpoint and shape variations, a uniform translation is the sum of its endpoint variations and the swept-strip area variation. With antisymmetric area convention this has the form \(\partial_{C,\mu}=\partial_{x,\mu}+\partial_{y,\mu}+\int_C dz^\alpha\,\delta/\delta\sigma^{\alpha\mu}(z)\). Vanishing of the left side gives the identity used for translation-invariant functionals, with endpoint conventions retained.
reconstruction: This is a variational identity on a specified domain, not an operator identity for arbitrary functions on curves. The sign in (20) uses antisymmetry of the two-form index.
fate: This is an elementary shape-variation identity in the area/path calculus already used by \citet[Eqs.~(12)--(14)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}. The notation in \citet[Sec.~4.3]{makeenko2000large} is a partial match; neither source was verified to print the exact open-path form (19).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A conditional shape-variation formula; no independent open problem is stated.

title: The classical Yang--Mills equation in loop notation
notes: From \(D_\mu F_{\mu\nu}=0\), formulas (15), (15\textquotesingle) and (24) obtain \(\partial^x_\mu\delta\Psi/\delta\sigma_{\mu\nu}(x)=0\). Formulas (21)--(23) invoke the curvature-squared action.
statement:
For a smooth solution of the source-free Yang--Mills equation on a Euclidean domain, the marked path derivative of the curvature-inserted Wilson loop vanishes: \(\partial^x_\mu\delta W(C)/\delta\sigma_{\mu
u}(x)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}((D_\mu F_{\mu
u})U(C_x))=0\). With \(S= eta\int\operatorname{Tr}F_{\mu
u}F_{\mu
u}\) summed over ordered indices and trace-pairing convention, variation gives \(\delta S/\delta A_
u=-4 eta D_\mu F_{\mu
u}\); alternate action normalization changes the prefactor.
reconstruction: The notebook (23) has mismatched free indices and suppresses the action-dependent prefactor and sign. Only the zero set is unaffected by an overall nonzero factor.
fate: \citet[Eq.~(14), followed by Eqs.~(16)--(18)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact} identifies the classical loop derivative before January 1980. The modern account is \citet[Sec.~4.3]{makeenko2000large}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. It does not identify the quantum large-rank equation with the classical Yang--Mills equation.

title: Normalized expectation and the weak Schwinger--Dyson identity
notes: (25) displays adjacent integrals for the expectation; (26)--(28) integrate a functional derivative and replace the classical equation by \(\hbar\delta/\delta A\).
statement: For a finite-dimensional regulator with density \(Z^{-1}e^{-S(a)/\hbar}\,da\), integrable \(Q\) and vanishing boundary terms, \(\langle(\partial_jS)Q\rangle=\hbar\langle\partial_jQ\rangle\). The continuum expression is formal until a regulator, measure, gauge treatment and renormalization are specified. The equality with a differential operator holds inside expectations, not as equality of ordinary functions.
reconstruction: The partition function in (25) must divide the numerator. The required decay/domain assumptions are not in the notebook.
fate: The weak field-equation replacement and normalized lattice expectation already occur in \citet[Eqs.~(16), (21)--(22)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}; \citet[Eqs.~(135)--(136)]{makeenko2000large} makes the integration-by-parts interpretation explicit.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A rigorous integration-by-parts identity for appropriate regulators, and a formal continuum identity unless independently justified.

title: The color contraction is specific to the defining unitary representation
notes: (31)--(33) split the transport at an insertion and claim a two-trace contraction for an arbitrary semisimple group, with the correction \(-N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(UV)\).
statement:
For traceless Hermitian generators of \(\mathfrak{su}(N)\) normalized by \(\operatorname{Tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}\), completeness gives
\[
\sum_a(T^a)_{ij}(T^a)_{kl}
=\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}-N^{-1}\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sum_a\operatorname{Tr}(T^aUT^aV)
=\operatorname{Tr}U\operatorname{Tr}V-N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(UV).
\]
Adding the normalized identity generator gives the \(U(N)\) version without the subtraction.
reconstruction: The group, defining representation, and trace normalization are essential. The formula is not valid unchanged for every semisimple group.
fate: The defining-representation color projection is explicit in \citet[Eq.~(16)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}, published December 1979, and in \citet[Sec.~4.2 and Eq.~(157)]{makeenko2000large}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An exact finite-dimensional identity in the stated convention. The notebook	extquotesingle s unrestricted group quantifier is false.

title: Finite-rank loop equations form a hierarchy
notes: Equation (34) relates the derivative of one loop expectation to a two-loop expectation. The notes correctly say that one loop is insufficient and include self-intersections.
statement: Writing \(W(C)=N^{-1}\langle\operatorname{Tr}U(C)\rangle\), the formal \(SU(N)\) equation in a conventional coupling normalization is \[\partial^x_\mu\frac{\delta W(C)}{\delta\sigma_{\mu\nu}(x)}=\lambda\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)\left(W_2(C_{xy},C_{yx})-\frac{1}{N^2}W(C)\right).\] Here \(W_2=\langle N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}U(C_{xy})\,N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}U(C_{yx})\rangle\). Higher products generate a splitting/joining hierarchy.
reconstruction: The \(SU(N)\) subtraction, trace normalization and coupling are restored. Contact terms and coincident points require a regulator.
fate: \citet[Eqs.~(16)--(19)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}, received 17 September and published 3 December 1979, already gives the finite-rank two-trace equation and explains its lack of closure. \citet[Eqs.~(157), (161)]{makeenko2000large} supplies the higher hierarchy explicitly.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The formal hierarchy is established; rigorous results are available in specified regulated and lower-dimensional settings, not an unrestricted four-dimensional continuum theorem.

title: Gauge-covariant regularization must reconnect separated endpoints
notes: The notes warn that simply smoothing \(\delta(x-y)\) opens the two contours; smoothing must be accompanied by closing them.
statement: When \(x\ne y\) in a point-split color contraction, open transports transform at different endpoints. To preserve gauge invariance one must include connecting parallel transports (and specify their paths), or use a gauge-invariant lattice regulator. A scalar mollifier alone cannot turn the separated open factors into gauge-invariant Wilson loops.
reconstruction: We spell out the endpoint transformation argument. The notes give no complete regularization prescription or convergence theorem.
fate: A gauge-invariant lattice equation is already given in \citet[Eqs.~(20)--(23)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact}, after the singular contact term is discussed. \citet[Sec.~4.6]{makeenko2000large} gives later continuum regularizations. The endpoint-covariance constraint is elementary; these later constructions are not dated to 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A valid methodological constraint; existence of a continuum limit is a separate problem.

title: Large-rank factorization requires normalized traces
notes: (35) states \(\langle\Psi(C_1)\cdots\Psi(C_m)\rangle=\prod_i\langle\Psi(C_i)\rangle+O(N^{-2})\), then observes \(\Psi(0)=N\) and redefines \(\Psi=N\bar\Phi\).
statement: For fixed loops, normalized single-trace observables \(\Phi=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}U\), fixed \(\lambda=g^2N\), and a regime admitting the usual topological expansion, \(\langle\Phi_1\cdots\Phi_m\rangle-\prod_i\langle\Phi_i\rangle=O(N^{-2})\). For the unnormalized \(\Psi_i\), the corresponding absolute error is \(O(N^{m-2})\). Factorization is an additional dynamical large-rank assertion, not a consequence of gauge invariance alone.
reconstruction: The order estimate in (35) is moved to the normalized variables introduced immediately below it. The topological-expansion regime is explicit.
fate: \citet[Eq.~(19)]{makeenkomigdal1979exact} explicitly states factorization with normalized traces before the talk. Its perturbative topological counting is rooted in \citet[Sec.~3, Eqs.~(3.2)--(3.7)]{thooft1974planar}, received December 1973 and published April 1974. \citet[Sec.~3.4 and Eqs.~(158)--(160)]{makeenko2000large} is the later detailed account.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard in perturbation theory and specified lattice regimes; the literal normalization in (35) is inconsistent.

title: The general confinement goal and the proposed large-rank route
notes: The notes say the \(SU(\infty)\) theory is near an exact solution and conclude that the equation for \(\bar\Phi\) gives \ru{confinement}. No solution, positivity criterion, uniqueness argument, continuum limit or area-law proof is supplied.
statement: A definite modern version asks for the physically selected, renormalized four-dimensional pure \(SU(N)\) Yang--Mills Wilson-loop expectations in the large-\(N\) limit, satisfying the loop equation, positivity and normalization, and a positive string tension in the large rectangular-loop limit. Closure of an equation alone neither constructs that solution nor proves its area law.
reconstruction: The notebook\textquotesingle s broad assertion is not a fully formulated theorem. The explicit pure-gauge, dimension, limit and positivity conditions define the identifiable confinement programme, rather than claiming those words were all spoken.
fate: \citet[abstract]{wilson1974confinement} proves a strong-coupling lattice mechanism; \citet[main theorem]{chatterjee2015string} proves a rigorous large-rank lattice/string correspondence for \(SO(N)\) at strong coupling. These do not settle the continuum assertion. The continuing four-dimensional construction problem is described in \citet[problem statement]{jaffewitten2000yangmills}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Partly developed. Controlled lattice and two-dimensional results do not constitute a general solution of four-dimensional continuum confinement from the loop equations.
worth: A sharply regulated special case can be worthwhile, but the unrestricted continuum confinement programme is not a plausible bounded contribution for this chapter.

title: Coxeter presentations, reduced words and Bruhat order
