notes: Equations (1)--(3) define a Coxeter group and reduced words, and define the elements \(<w\) by deleting any subset of a reduced expression. Examples are symmetric and Weyl groups; the symmetric-group discussion displays only the neighboring braid relation.
statement: Let \((W,S)\) be a Coxeter system with finite \(S\), exponents \(m(s,s)=1\), and \(m(s,t)\in\{2,3,\ldots,\infty\}\) for \(s\ne t\); no relation is imposed for exponent \(\infty\). The length is the least number of generators. The Bruhat relation \(y\le w\) holds exactly when a reduced expression for \(w\) has a subword whose product is \(y\); this does not depend on the chosen reduced expression. In \(S_n\), also require \(s_i s_j=s_j s_i\) for \(|i-j|>1\).
reconstruction: The empty deletion gives \(y=w\), so the general relation is \(\le\), not strict \(<\). The omitted distant commutations are needed for the symmetric-group presentation.
fate: The talk\textquotesingle s named source is \citet[Sec.~1]{kazhdanlusztig1979representations}, received March and published June 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard Coxeter theory; the two qualifications prevent literal misreadings of the compressed examples.

title: The Hecke algebra, specialization and its standard basis
notes: Equations (4)--(6) impose \((T_s+1)(T_s-q)=0\) and braid relations, note specialization \(q=1\), identify the finite-field double-coset algebra, and define \(T_w\) using a reduced word.
statement: Over \(A=\mathbb Z[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}]\), the equal-parameter Hecke algebra \(\mathcal H(W)\) has basis \(T_w\), with products along reduced expressions independent of the expression. Under \(q^{1/2}\mapsto1\) it becomes \(\mathbb Z[W]\). For a split finite reductive group over \(\mathbb F_q\) with Borel subgroup \(B\), the complex specialization is the algebra of \(B\)-bi-invariant functions, with convolution normalized so \(1_B\) is the identity and the double-coset generators satisfy the stated quadratic relation.
reconstruction: The tensor product with \(\mathbb C\) needs the specialization homomorphism. Splitness, equal parameters and convolution normalization are not written out in the notes.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{kazhdanlusztig1979representations} is the explicit pre-talk source.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. Unequal-parameter or twisted finite groups require a modified statement.

title: Bar involution and inversion of Hecke generators
statement: There is a semilinear algebra involution of \(\mathcal H\), semilinear over the involution \(q^{1/2}\mapsto q^{-1/2}\), determined by \(\overline{T_s}=T_s^{-1}\). The quadratic relation implies the displayed inverse, and the braid relations ensure well-definedness. Thus \(\overline{T_w}=T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}\).
reconstruction: It is semilinear, not \(A\)-linear; the inverse in the subscript formula is distinguished from inversion of \(w\).
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{kazhdanlusztig1979representations}; the generator calculation is supplied in the notebook itself.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An exact algebraic construction.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the Kazhdan--Lusztig basis
notes:
\ru{Теорема 1.1}: a unique bar-invariant element has the expansion
\[
C^{\prime}_w=q^{-\ell(w)/2}\sum_{y\le w}P_{y,w}T_y,
\]
with \(P_{w,w}=1\) and the strict degree bound (12).
statement: For every Coxeter system and every \(w\in W\), there is a unique \(C^{\prime}_w=q^{-\ell(w)/2}\sum_{y\le w}P_{y,w}(q)T_y\) such that \(\overline{C^{\prime}_w}=C^{\prime}_w\), \(P_{w,w}=1\), \(P_{y,w}\in\mathbb Z[q]\), and \(\deg P_{y,w}\le(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2\) for \(y<w\). These elements form an \(A\)-basis.
reconstruction: For \(y\not\le w\), set \(P_{y,w}=0\). The bound is interpreted integrally and the zero polynomial is allowed.
fate: The source and theorem number match \citet[Thm.~1.1]{kazhdanlusztig1979representations}, published in 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for arbitrary Coxeter systems. This algebraic existence theorem is separate from geometric positivity or character formulas.

title: The simple-reflection polynomial and the second canonical basis
notes: The calculation gives \(C^{\prime}_s=q^{-1/2}(T_s+1)\), \(P_{e,s}=P_{s,s}=1\); (16) defines \(C_w=\varepsilon_wj(C^{\prime}_w)\).
statement: The semilinear involution \(j\) is specified by \(j(q^{1/2})=q^{-1/2}\) and \(j(T_w)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}q^{-\ell(w)}T_w\). It gives the alternative basis \(C_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}j(C^{\prime}_w)\). In rank one, \(C_s=q^{-1/2}T_s-q^{1/2}\), and direct substitution verifies both bar invariance and \(T_sC_s=-C_s\).
reconstruction: The last expression and direct check are elementary consequences clarifying the sign convention; they are not a claimed new result.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{kazhdanlusztig1979representations} uses these two conventions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Exact; the two bases must not be interchanged in the multiplication formula.

title: Kazhdan--Lusztig multiplicities of Verma modules
notes: (13), twice labelled \ru{гипотеза}, states \([M_w:L_y]=P_{w_0w,w_0y}(1)\), with \(L_w\) the simple quotient and \(y\le w\). The notes say it has been checked for \(\mathrm{GL}(4)\).
statement: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, choose a Borel and Cartan, and let \(\lambda\) be a regular integral antidominant weight for the dot action. Put \(M_w=M(w\cdot\lambda)\), and let \(L_w\) be its simple quotient, all in the corresponding block of category \(\mathcal O\). Then \([M_w:L_y]=P_{w_0w,w_0y}(1)\) for \(y\le w\), and the multiplicity is zero otherwise.
reconstruction: The regular integral block and antidominant indexing are absent from the notebook and are essential to this exact indexing. The isolated \(\mathrm{GL}(4)\) check is reported as historical notebook evidence, not independently reconstructed.
fate: Proved independently by \citet{brylinskikashiwara1981holonomic} and \citet{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}. \citet[pp.~43--44]{brylinski1981differential}, reporting the 1980 Toru\'n lectures, explicitly records both proofs before their 1981 publication.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A theorem in the stated characteristic-zero category. The 1980 note accurately distinguishes the then-conjectural multiplicities from the 1979 basis theorem.

title: Vogan parity and the Ext-polynomial refinement
notes: (14)--(15) give \(P_{y,w}=\sum_{i\ge0}q^i\dim\operatorname{Ext}^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)-2i}(M_y,L_w)\) and vanishing in the other parity, attributed to Vogan.
statement: With the same regular integral antidominant indexing in category \(\mathcal O\), for \(y\le w\) the dimensions satisfy \[P_{y,w}(q)=\sum_{i\ge0}q^i\dim\operatorname{Ext}^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)-2i}_{\mathcal O}(M_y,L_w),\] taking negative Ext degrees to be zero, and \(\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal O}(M_y,L_w)=0\) unless \(j\equiv\ell(w)-\ell(y)\pmod2\). Equivalently these are the appropriate weight spaces of nilradical cohomology.
reconstruction: The category, block, and indexing convention must be fixed; unrestricted Ext over all \(U(\mathfrak g)\)-modules is not the stated formula.
fate: \citet[Conj.~3.4 and Thm.~3.5]{vogan1979irreducible} states the equivalent nilradical-cohomology refinement; received 16 July and published December 1979. Its geometric proof belongs to the same 1980--1981 resolution recorded by \citet[pp.~43--44]{brylinski1981differential}. The exact category-\(\mathcal O\) Ext formula in this normalization is also printed in \citet[p.~262]{gabberjoseph1981towards}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established under these hypotheses. The coefficient formula gives more information than evaluating at \(q=1\); its equivalence to the character conjecture uses additional structure.

title: Multiplication in the canonical basis and cell subquotients
notes: Equation (17) defines the leading coefficient \(\mu\); \ru{Теорема 1.3}, equation (18), gives the action of \(T_s\). The final sentence says the regular representation becomes block triangular.
statement: Let \(\mu(z,v)\) be the coefficient of \(q^{(\ell(v)-\ell(z)-1)/2}\) in \(P_{z,v}\), set to zero when that degree is not a nonnegative integer or \(z\not<v\). Then \[T_sC_v=\begin{cases}-C_v,&sv<v,\\qC_v+q^{1/2}C_{sv}+q^{1/2}\sum_{z<v,\,sz<z}\mu(z,v)C_z,&sv>v.\end{cases}\] The associated preorder yields invariant filtrations and left-cell subquotients of the regular representation. Cell modules are not asserted to be irreducible in every Coxeter type.
reconstruction: The zero convention for \(\mu\) makes the notebook sum well-defined. The phrase block triangular is interpreted as a filtration, not a canonical direct-sum decomposition into irreducibles.
fate: \citet[Thm.~1.3 and the cell construction]{kazhdanlusztig1979representations}; this was already published in June 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. The formula is for \(C_v\), not \(C^{\prime}_v\).

title: Allowable chains for middle intersection homology
notes: (3)--(4) use an even-dimensional filtration and cycles meeting \(X_{n-2c}\) in dimension \(i-c-1\); bounding chains have the bound \(i-c\). The notes mention local topological triviality along strata.
statement: Let \(X\) be a pure real \(n\)-dimensional stratified PL pseudomanifold with locally conical structure and no codimension-one stratum. For middle perversity \(\bar m(k)=\lfloor(k-2)/2\rfloor\), the allowable-chain complex consists of PL chains \(\xi\) satisfying \(\dim(|\xi|\cap X_{n-k})\le i-k+\bar m(k)\) and the analogous boundary bound \(\dim(|\partial\xi|\cap X_{n-k})\le i-1-k+\bar m(k)\). Its homology is \(IH_i^{\bar m}(X;\mathbb Q)\). For codimension \(2c\), the first bound is \(i-c-1\).
reconstruction: The inequalities, boundary condition, coefficient field and conical pseudomanifold hypotheses are supplied. Equality of dimensions is neither required nor correct.
fate: Already announced in \citet[definition and propositions]{goreskymacpherson1977dualite}; the full chain treatment appears in \citet[Sec.~1]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. The chain complex, not an unconstrained quotient of all bounding chains, is the precise object.

title: Smooth normalization and rational Poincare duality
notes: (1) gives \(IH_i(X)=H_i(X)\) when \(X\) is nonsingular; (2) pairs \(IH_i\) with \(IH_{n-i}\) into \(\mathbb Q\), with an unexplained superscript-like mark.
statement: For a manifold the allowable conditions are vacuous, so intersection homology agrees with ordinary homology. For a compact oriented stratified pseudomanifold, complementary perversities \(\bar p(k)+\bar q(k)=k-2\) admit a nondegenerate rational pairing \(IH_i^{\bar p}(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes IH_{n-i}^{\bar q}(X;\mathbb Q)\to\mathbb Q\). If all strata have even codimension, middle perversity is self-complementary and gives the notebook\textquotesingle s same-perversity pairing.
reconstruction: Compactness, orientation, rational coefficients and even codimensions are necessary qualifications. No interpretation is forced on the stray superscript. For noncompact spaces use the appropriate compact-support/Borel--Moore pairing.
fate: \citet[duality theorem]{goreskymacpherson1977dualite}; detailed proof in \citet[Sec.~3.3]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established with these hypotheses. Integral perfect duality does not follow in general.

title: Schubert closures supply the relevant even stratification
notes: The note first says strange cohomology of Schubert cells, then explicitly writes \ru{шуберт. кл. (замкн.)} and uses smaller cells as the strata.
statement: For a connected complex reductive group \(G\), Borel \(B\), Weyl group \(W\), and \(t\in W\), set \(X_t=\overline{BtB/B}\subset G/B\). Its Bruhat cells \(BsB/B\), \(s\le t\), are smooth affine complex spaces of dimensions \(\ell(s)\); they give the even real-dimensional stratification used for the local intersection-cohomology construction.
reconstruction: The singular space is a Schubert variety, the closure of a cell. An open Bruhat cell itself is smooth and cannot carry the claimed singularity information.
fate: The geometric theorem is \citet{kazhdanlusztig1980schubert}, published in 1980. A primary contemporary witness, \citet[p.~261, footnote; p.~301, reference~11]{gabberjoseph1981towards}, explicitly cites the Harvard 1979 preprint and distinguishes its solved geometric problem from the later character-formula proofs. Thus the 1980 publication date does not make this a development after the January talk. The original KL proof itself was not retrieved.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The closure/open-cell distinction is essential.

title: Local intersection cohomology computes Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials
notes: (5) writes \(P_{s,t}(q)=q^{?}\sum_i\dim IH_i(X_t,X_t-y_s)q^i\). The exponent is literally a question mark; the use of special characteristic-\(p\) cohomology is mentioned.
statement: For \(s\le t\) in the Weyl group of a complex reductive group, let \(IC_{X_t}\) be the rational intersection-cohomology complex normalized to restrict to \(\mathbb Q[\ell(t)]\) on the open cell. At \(y_s\) in the \(s\)-cell, \[P_{s,t}(q)=\sum_{j\ge0}\dim\mathcal H^{2j-\ell(t)}(IC_{X_t})_{y_s}\,q^j.\] Stalk degrees of the opposite parity vanish. This is a local stalk formula, not the ordinary or global Poincare polynomial of \(X_t\).
reconstruction: The displayed formula is an editorial modern normalization, replacing the visibly unfinished homological notation. No value is silently inserted for the original question mark; homological local groups require duality and indexing translations.
fate: The geometric theorem is \citet{kazhdanlusztig1980schubert}, published in 1980. A primary contemporary witness, \citet[p.~261, footnote; p.~301, reference~11]{gabberjoseph1981towards}, explicitly cites the Harvard 1979 preprint and distinguishes its solved geometric problem from the later character-formula proofs. Thus the 1980 publication date does not make this a development after the January talk. The original KL proof itself was not retrieved.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established characteristic-zero geometric interpretation. The notebook records the theorem with an unresolved grading convention.

title: The Gaussian family with orthogonal-group labels
notes: (1)--(3) display \(G=\bigcup GL(n,\mathbb R)\), \(K=\bigcup SO(n)\), and \(T_{\pi_1,s_1;\ldots;\pi_r,s_r}\), where \(\pi_i\in\widehat{O(n_i)}\) and \(s_i\in\mathbb R\).
statement: For the Gaussian quasi-regular representation \(T_s\) of the finite-matrix group \(SL(\infty,\mathbb R)\) on \(L^2(\mathbb R^{\mathbb N},\mu)\), the commutant of \(T_s^{\otimes n}\) is generated by the natural \(O(n)\) action mixing the rows. Its \(O(n)\)-isotypic multiplicity spaces carry irreducible representations \(T_{\pi,s}\). For pairwise distinct real parameters \(s_i\), \(\bigotimes_iT_{\pi_i,s_i}\) is irreducible and determines the unordered parameter family. These representations extend to the polar completion \(GL(\infty,\mathbb R)=UR\), where \(U\) has the strong operator topology and \(R\) consists of positive invertible operators \(1+A\) with \(A\) Hilbert--Schmidt, with its Hilbert--Schmidt topology.
reconstruction: The Gaussian model, extension topology and distinctness condition are reconstructed from the identified publication. The notebook gives only the parameter list, not a classification of all abstract representations of the algebraic union.
fate: Exact family in \citet[Secs.~3 and 5, Thms.~5--7]{olshanskii1980construction}; presented 21 June and received 25 June 1979, published in volume 250(2), 1980. The exact issue-release day relative to 4 February was not verified. The result was already formulated in the note presented in June 1979; this is treated as contemporary exposition, not as a post-seminar first discovery. The precise public release day of the 1980 issue remains unverified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A proved contemporary construction. The A label identifies the speaker	extquotesingle s 1980 publication; it does not imply that the manuscript first circulated after the seminar.

title: Discrete finite-multiplicity restriction and the maximal-compact analogy
notes: The family restricts to \(K\) with \ru{конечнокр. дискр. спектр}; the notes call \(K\) analogous to a maximal compact subgroup and mention a unitary variant.
statement: For these Gaussian finite-row representations, orthogonal transformations of the countably many columns preserve the Gaussian measure, so the restriction is independent of the parameters \(s_i\). Its Hilbert decomposition into continuous tensor-type \(SO(\infty)\) representations is discrete, with finite multiplicities. The complex construction replaces real Gaussian space and \(O(n_i)\) labels by their complex/unitary counterparts. The union \(SO(\infty)\) is not itself a compact group.
reconstruction: The assertion is restricted to the family displayed in the notes and to its continuous tensor category; it is not a Peter--Weyl theorem for all representations of an arbitrary inductive-limit topology.
fate: \citet[Sec.~3 and the proof of Thm.~6]{olshanskii1980construction} supplies the Gaussian model and its compact dual; compare the decomposition under restriction in \citet[Sec.~1]{olshanskii1978unitary}. The result was formulated in the note presented in June 1979, so the talk is treated as contemporary exposition. The precise public release day of the 1980 issue remains unverified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in this representation class. The maximal-compact phrase is an analogy about restriction theory.

title: Type I for the completed finite-real-rank groups
notes: (4)--(6) put closure bars over the unions \(SO(p,n)\), \(U(p,n)\), \(Sp(p,n)\), call them completions, and state that they are type I.
statement: Fix finite \(p\). Use Olshanskii\textquotesingle s operator completions of \(SO_0(p,\infty)\), \(U(p,\infty)\), and \(Sp(p,\infty)\), not the discrete group or an unspecified final topology. Every continuous unitary representation generates a type-I von Neumann algebra; there are no factor representations of type II or III. In the norm/strong formulations specified by the paper, the continuous representation categories agree.
reconstruction: The identity component \(SO_0\), Hilbert-space continuity and completion topology are supplied. Type I refers to the generated operator algebra of every continuous unitary representation.
fate: \citet[Thm.~3.3]{olshanskii1978unitary}; received 20 October 1977, published 1978. The 1980 paper explicitly credits this earlier result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for the stated completions. Changing the topology changes the assertion.

title: Exhaustion of finite-rank irreducibles by holomorphic constructions
notes: The same sentence says that all irreducible representations of the completed fixed-\(p\) groups have been described.
statement: For the completed groups in the preceding item, the 1980 classification uses irreducible holomorphic representations of a specified \(\mathbb Z\)-cover of \(U(p,\infty)\). Their restrictions produce the irreducibles of \(SO_0(p,\infty)\) and, from \(U(2p,\infty)\), of \(Sp(p,\infty)\); holomorphic--antiholomorphic tensor products give the unitary case. The admissible highest-weight pairs in Theorems 1--2 determine the parameters. For the un-covered \(U(p,\infty)\), retain precisely the representations on which the covering kernel acts trivially.
reconstruction: The cover, admissibility and descent condition are absent from the one-line notebook summary. We state the classification mechanism, not an unsupported claim for arbitrary representations of the algebraic union.
fate: \citet[Thms.~1--4]{olshanskii1980construction} proves the exhaustion; manuscript June 1979, publication 1980. The 1978 paper proves type I and constructs many representations but does not claim this full exhaustion. The result was already formulated in the note presented in June 1979; this is treated as contemporary exposition, not as a post-seminar first discovery. The precise public release day of the 1980 issue remains unverified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated continuous category; the two chronology layers are kept separate.

title: Locally linear flattenings are an additional triangulation hypothesis
notes: \(X\) is a simplicial four-manifold, and for every simplex \(\sigma\) the notes assume \(\psi:\operatorname{St}\sigma\to\mathbb R^4\), linear on simplices and homeomorphic near the interior of \(\sigma\). A two-dimensional sketch illustrates the star.
statement: Work with a finite triangulated PL four-manifold, with a local flattening of each simplex: a simplicewise affine map from its star to \(\mathbb R^4\) that is a homeomorphism on a neighborhood of the relative interior. Equivalently, the normal cone on the link of a codimension-\(k\) simplex has an appropriate linear flattening in \(\mathbb R^k\). This condition is imposed on the triangulation; it is not inferred merely from the word PL.
reconstruction: The normal-space formulation explains the later dependence on codimension. A chosen triangulation of a PL manifold need not automatically satisfy this particular linear-star condition.
fate: \citet[pp.~105--106]{macpherson1978combinatorial}; exposition February 1977, publication 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A precise hypothesis of the construction, not a new 1980 assertion of universal linear realizability.

title: The hypersimplex over a simplex and its elementary models
notes: (5)--(6) prescribe \(h(v)\in[0,1]\), \(h=1\) on vertices of \(\sigma\), and \(\sum_vh(v)=5\). Examples are a point, a segment, a triangle and an octahedron. Vertices are labelled by the places where \(h=1\).
statement: For a simplex \(\sigma\) in a closed four-manifold, let \(V_\sigma\) be the vertex set of its star and put \[H_\sigma=\{h\in[0,1]^{V_\sigma}:h|_{V(\sigma)}=1,\ \sum h=5\}.\] If \(\sigma\) has codimension \(k\), the remaining coordinates sum to \(k\). All vertices are zero--one functions. Thus a top-dimensional simplex gives a point; a codimension-one simplex gives a segment. For codimension two, three remaining vertices give \(\Delta(2,3)\), a triangle, and four give \(\Delta(2,4)\), an octahedron.
reconstruction: The notebook uses two-dimensional pictures for four-dimensional normal combinatorics. The exact cube slice is \(\sum h_i=2\), not an arbitrary equidistant cutting plane.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{macpherson1978combinatorial}; compare the earlier seminar occurrence 1976-413.10.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An elementary convex-polytope construction. Boundary simplices require a relative variant of the segment example.

title: Gluing the hypersimplicial space over the original complex
notes: For \(\sigma\subset\sigma^{\prime}\), the notes put \(H_{\sigma^{\prime}}\subset H_\sigma\), identify the common part \(H_{\sigma^{\prime}}\times\sigma\), and glue the products. They also draw the original and dual cell structures.
statement: Extend a function on \(V_{\sigma^{\prime}}\) by zero to \(V_\sigma\); this embeds \(H_{\sigma^{\prime}}\) as a face of \(H_\sigma\). Glue the products \(H_\sigma\times\sigma\) along these face inclusions to obtain \(H\to X\). Use the barycentric/common subdivision \(X^{\prime}\) when comparing the primal simplex cells with the dual cells \(\sigma^D\); cellular means that each skeleton maps into the corresponding skeleton.
reconstruction: The extension-by-zero rule and the common subdivision make the arrows in the notebook unambiguous.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established; incidence reverses under passage from simplices to dual cells.

title: Configuration spaces and their degeneracy loci
notes: \(C_\sigma\) first means all flattenings \(\psi\). General position requires every set consisting of all vertices of \(\sigma\) and \(k\) other star vertices, five points in total, to be independent. Speciality \(c\) counts the failures.
statement: For a codimension-\(k\) simplex, pass to normal flattenings of the cone on its link in \(\mathbb R^k\), modulo \(GL(k,\mathbb R)\). A configuration is generic if each relevant \(k\)-subset of link vertices has nonzero determinant. The \(c\)-fold degeneracy locus has exactly \(c\) zero determinants. It is semialgebraic and has finitely many connected components. In the original four-space, these are the affine-independence tests on the displayed five points.
reconstruction: The normal quotient and the word exactly are supplied. The notes subsequently reuse \(C_\sigma\) for a finite cell model; the raw realization space and that model are distinct.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A precise finite semialgebraic construction. No assertion that all its connected pieces are balls follows from the definition.

title: Does the degeneracy decomposition itself form a cell structure?
notes: After defining speciality, the recorder writes:\par\ru{Неизвестно: стратификация или клет. разбиение}.
statement: The identifiable issue is whether the degeneracy pieces of the raw flattening quotient, or their connected components, have the topology and incidence properties of cells. The notes do not specify which decomposition, whether a refinement is allowed, or what notion of stratification is intended. Therefore they do not determine a unique yes/no theorem.
reconstruction: This uncertainty is retained rather than converted into a blanket conjecture about all realization spaces. Semialgebraic refinement and the separately constructed finite complex answer different questions.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2]{macpherson1978combinatorial} explicitly constructs a cell complex from components; it does not identify every raw component with an open cell.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: No exact standalone problem can be recovered from this sentence. It is not evidence that the whole Pontryagin construction remained undeveloped.

title: The low-codimension configuration cell models
notes: For \(k=4\), one point is assigned to every generic component; for \(k=3\), walls of speciality one produce edges; for \(k=2\), speciality-two components give squares. The later point case mistakenly repeats \(k=2\).
statement: Write \(K_\sigma\) for the finite model. For codimension four it is a discrete set. For codimension three it is the graph with vertices the generic components and an edge for each connected one-degeneracy wall, joining the two adjacent components. For codimension two fill the four-cycle around a two-degeneracy component by a square. For codimension one or zero put \(K_\sigma=\{*\}\). Crossing one determinant wall changes a sign, hence its two endpoints are distinct and no loop edge arises.
reconstruction: The notation \(K_\sigma\) separates the model from the raw configuration space. The second point-case index must be zero, not two.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2, pp.~109--111]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The stated finite construction is established. It is not a theorem that arbitrary higher-codimension realization spaces have such a simple cell decomposition.

title: Connectivity of the codimension-three configuration graph
notes: The first line says \ru{Граф связен (трудная теорема!)}.
statement: For a codimension-three simplex in the locally flattenable triangulated manifold under consideration, the configuration graph described in the preceding item is connected: generic local flattenings can be joined by passages through one-degeneracy walls.
reconstruction: The assertion is about this local-star graph. It is not a general connectivity claim for all oriented-matroid realization spaces.
fate: \citet[Note~2, p.~122]{macpherson1978combinatorial} explicitly supplies the connectivity justification via Cairns\textquotesingle s 1944 isotopy theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the indicated setting; the difficult step was already available before the talk.

title: Restriction maps glue the configuration models
notes: The margin asks whether the \(C_\sigma\times\sigma^D\) glue naturally; the next lines restrict \(\psi\) from a larger star to a smaller one and draw \(C_{\sigma^{\prime}}\to C_\sigma\) when \(\sigma^{\prime}\subset\sigma\).
statement: If \(\sigma^{\prime}\subset\sigma\), restriction followed by projection to the corresponding normal quotient induces a map of configuration spaces and of the finite cell models \(K_{\sigma^{\prime}}\to K_\sigma\). These compatible maps glue the products with dual cells to a cellular space \(C\to X^D\). Using \(X^{\prime}\), it can be combined with \(H\to X\).
reconstruction: The normal projection, needed because codimension changes, is implicit in the notebook word restriction. The question is answered immediately by the construction rather than left as a newly open problem.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. This is related to the compatibility theme of 1976-413.11 but does not restate a new unsolved boundary-chain problem.

title: The compatible product complex Gamma
notes: The notes draw \(\Gamma\subset H\times_XC\). The bottom of P000911 says a product is included when the five-point configurations specified by vertices of the hypersimplex face are generic.
statement: Over the common subdivision, retain a product cell of the hypersimplicial and configuration factors only when every basis-sized subset indicated by a vertex of its hypersimplex face is nondegenerate for the corresponding flattening component. The resulting compatible cell subcomplex \(\Gamma\) has a projection \(\pi:\Gamma\to X\). Its allowed incidences make the characteristic cocycle well-defined.
reconstruction: The handwritten membership description is compressed; the criterion is supplied in the vocabulary of the published construction. It does not imply that every product cell is admissible.
fate: \citet[Sec.~3]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established compatibility construction; the projection is not claimed to be an ordinary fiber bundle.

title: The signed one-forty-eighth cocycle on four-cells
notes: The four face types have five variable coordinates and respectively three, two, one or zero additional coordinates fixed at one, above a vertex of \(X\). The two extreme types have value zero; the middle types have \(\widetilde P=\pm1/48\), with sign \((-1)^i\) from ten orientations.
statement: For an oriented four-cell lying over a vertex, a four-dimensional hypersimplex face has five varying coordinates and \(b=0,1,2,3\) other coordinates fixed at one besides the base vertex. The varying coordinates sum to \(4-b\), giving \(\Delta(4,5),\Delta(3,5),\Delta(2,5),\Delta(1,5)\). The characteristic cochain vanishes on the extreme types and on the other prescribed four-cells. On the middle types project the five varying vertices along the fixed span to \(\mathbb R^2\) or \(\mathbb R^3\). With the cell orientation determined by their ordering, its value is \((-1)^i/48\), where \(i\) counts positively oriented ordered pairs or triples among the ten relevant minors.
reconstruction: The base must be a vertex for this displayed fixed-coordinate count. Reversing the auxiliary orientation replaces \(i\) by \(10-i\), so the sign is unchanged; reversing the cell orientation reverses the value.
fate: \citet[Sec.~4]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An explicit rational cochain in the specified orientation convention. The normalization is not a universal assertion about all Pontryagin cocycle models.

title: The combinatorial cocycle represents the first Pontryagin class
notes: (4) says \(\pi^*p^1(X)=[\widetilde P]\), and the intervening construction is meant to produce \(\widetilde P\in C^4(\Gamma)\).
statement: Under the local flattening hypotheses, the prescribed cochain is a cocycle and \([\widetilde P]=\pi^*p_1(TX)\in H^4(\Gamma;\mathbb Q)\). A homological four-section \(s\) of \(\pi\) yields a representative \(s^*\widetilde P\) of \(p_1(X)\). Such a section is a chain map right-inverse through degree four; it is not necessarily a continuous section of \(\pi\).
reconstruction: The rational coefficients and homological-section interpretation explain how the pulled-back identity computes a class on \(X\). These details come from the publication, not an additional theorem claimed in the notebook.
fate: \citet[Sec.~3, Propositions~1--2; Sec.~4, theorem and Corollary~1]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Proved before 1980. The later all-Pontryagin formula of \citet{gelfandmacpherson1992combinatorial} is a broader development, not the publication date of this first-class formula.

title: Six coordinate degeneracy divisors on the real Grassmannian
notes: The notes mention six Schubert-cell closures, six coordinate two-planes in \(\mathbb R^4\), and planes nontransverse to each of them.
statement: For each coordinate two-plane \(E_I\subset\mathbb R^4\), the locus \(D_I=\{L\in\mathrm{Gr}(2,4):L\cap E_I\ne0\}\) is a Schubert degeneracy hypersurface for a flag containing \(E_I\). There are six such coordinate choices; their complement is the locus where all six Plucker coordinates are nonzero. Separately, the Schubert decomposition for one fixed full flag has six cells of dimensions \(0,1,2,2,3,4\). The six coordinate divisors are not those six cell closures.
reconstruction: The source compresses two uses of six. The distinction is supplied without silently equating the coordinate hypersurfaces with all cells for one flag.
fate: The Grassmannian/configuration setting is in \citet[Sec.~6]{macpherson1978combinatorial}; the precise generic-minor locus is also described in \citet[Secs.~3.1--3.3]{rojas2026explicit}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard incidence geometry. The notebook wording does not determine which full flags were intended.

title: Enhanced configurations of four rays and cross-ratio
notes: The English phrase says four points in \(\mathbb RP^2\), but the next lines and figure say four rays in \(\mathbb R^2\), ordinary points in \(\mathbb RP^1\), and \(\mathbb R^4/L\) for a two-plane \(L\). Configurations are equivalent under \(GL(2,\mathbb R)\).
statement: For \(L\in\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)\) with all relevant minors nonzero, the images of the four positive coordinate rays in \(\mathbb R^4/L\) are nonzero rays in a two-dimensional space. Up to linear isomorphism, they form an enhanced projective configuration: a projective-line configuration together with choices of lifts from lines to rays. For four distinct labelled projective points, an ordered cross-ratio is a complete continuous projective invariant; the ray choices add discrete data.
reconstruction: Projectivization has dimension one. The genericity condition excludes zero quotient vectors and coincident projective points. Cross-ratio alone does not encode all enhancement signs.
fate: \citet[Secs.~6--7]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. The configuration quotient may have non-Hausdorff boundary behavior; the generic interval components are sufficient for the cross-ratio discussion.

title: A Pontryagin form on the Grassmannian
notes: The notes label \(P\) a four-form representing the Pontryagin class of the standard rank-two bundle \(\xi\) on \(G_{2,2}(\mathbb R)\), and say that a connection is constructed.
statement: Let \(\xi\) be the tautological real two-plane bundle on \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)\), with the metric and projected connection induced from Euclidean space. Its Chern--Weil representative is \(P=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}(\Omega\wedge\Omega)\), where \(\Omega\) is the curvature. The de Rham class is \(p_1(\xi)\), independent of the connection. On the oriented double cover it equals the square of the Euler class.
reconstruction: The connection, curvature normalization and orientation-cover observation supply a precise version of the note. If instead one uses the quotient bundle under the complementary-plane identification, the corresponding sign/convention must be tracked.
fate: \citet[Secs.~5 and 8]{macpherson1978combinatorial} uses the invariant Grassmannian characteristic form.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Classical Chern--Weil theory; its later fiber integral is a different operation.

title: Fiber integration of the Pontryagin form and the Rogers dilogarithm
notes: The scan, more clearly than the linearized transcription, gives \(\bar\pi_*(P)=d\Phi\) and labels \(\Phi\) a function, \ru{дилогарифм}. The projection sends a two-plane to its enhanced four-ray configuration.
statement: On a generic component of the configuration quotient of \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)\), integration of the invariant first-Pontryagin four-form along the three-dimensional diagonal-scaling fibers, with the hypersimplicial compactification and an orientation convention, gives a one-form proportional to \(dL_R(x)\), where \(x\) is cross-ratio and \[L_R(x)=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Li}_2(x)+\tfrac12\log|x|\log|1-x|,\qquad x\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\}.\] Thus locally the fiber integral has a dilogarithmic primitive. Its scalar and additive constants depend on fiber/sign and normalization choices.
reconstruction: The source supplies neither the compactification nor a scalar normalization. The statement uses the real Rogers dilogarithm, not the Bloch--Wigner function; it does not silently assert an equality for an unspecified arbitrary connection.
fate: Developed by \citet[Secs.~0 and 3]{gelfandmacpherson1982geometry}, published June 1982. The full modern computation was read in \citet[Sec.~3.7 and Thm.~3.7, case \(k=1\)]{rojas2026explicit}, preprint 26 October 2026. The 1982 paper\textquotesingle s publisher metadata, not its full proof, was checked.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The first-class relation is established. The 2026 preprint supplies a new explicit treatment of powers of \(p_1\); its broader claims are not substituted for the notebook\textquotesingle s elementary case.

title: From a Grassmannian point to a vector and ray configuration
notes: \(G_{n,k}\) consists of unoriented \(n\)-planes in \(\mathbb R^{n+k}\); the text defines enhanced configurations of \(n+k\) points in \(k\)-space, parenthetically calling its projective dimension \(k+1\).
statement: For \(L\in\mathrm{Gr}(n,n+k)\), take the images of the coordinate vectors in \(V=\mathbb R^{n+k}/L\), of dimension \(k\), modulo linear isomorphisms of \(V\). The resulting spanning labelled vector configuration determines \(L\) as the kernel of the corresponding surjection \(\mathbb R^{n+k}\to V\). Passing to the images of positive coordinate rays forgets their positive lengths and gives an enhanced projective configuration; zero quotient vectors need a separate boundary stratum. Nonzero projective points lie in \(\mathbb RP^{k-1}\).
reconstruction: The kernel construction, generic/nonzero qualification, and dimension \(k-1\) are editorial clarification. The printed \(k+1\) is not retained as a mathematical claim.
fate: \citet[Sec.~6]{macpherson1978combinatorial}, exposition February 1977 and publication 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An exact quotient/configuration construction with the stated boundary qualification.

title: A configuration plus a hypersimplex point recovers the plane
notes: The fragment\textquotesingle s central line reads:\par\ru{Элементу} \(G_{n,k}\) \ru{соотв. пара гиперсимплекс + конфигурация}.
statement: Fix a spanning rank-\(k\) vector configuration \(w_1,\ldots,w_{n+k}\) and denote by \(\Delta_I\) its maximal minors. A convenient hypersimplicial coordinate is \[h_i=\frac{\sum_{I\ni i}|\Delta_I|}{\sum_{|I|=k}|\Delta_I|},\qquad0\le h_i\le1,\quad\sum_i h_i=k.\] On each effective orbit of positive independent coordinate rescalings, quotienting by its full stabilizer, this map is a homeomorphism onto the relative interior of the polytope spanned by the indicator vectors of subsets with \(\Delta_I\ne0\); its closure maps to that polytope. Thus the enhanced projective configuration and this point recover the Grassmannian datum. For a generic configuration the polytope is the full \(\Delta(k,n+k)\).
reconstruction: The explicit map, absolute-minor convention and non-generic face polytope come from the identified source, not the clipped continuation. Alternative moment-map normalizations using squared minors give related coordinates and are not conflated with this formula. In a nongeneric disconnected configuration, the stabilizer may be larger than common scalar multiplication; the assertion concerns the effective orbit in the Grassmannian, not the unreduced parameter torus.
fate: \citet[Sec.~6, proposition]{macpherson1978combinatorial}; the further Grassmannian development is \citet{gelfandmacpherson1982geometry}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the specified configuration/orbit formulation. The notebook does not formulate a new open question here.

title: Hydrostatic reduction of the incompressible free-surface equations
notes: The fluid occupies \(0<z<h(r,t)\), with horizontal velocity \(u\), vertical velocity \(w\), and \(w_z+\operatorname{div}u=0\). The vertical equation on P000915 has \(-p_z+1\), while P000916 writes \(p_z+1=0\) and obtains \(p=h-z\).
statement: For an inviscid incompressible fluid of constant density, a flat impermeable bed, gravitational acceleration scaled to one, and zero pressure at the surface, neglecting the entire vertical material acceleration gives \(p_z=-1\), hence \(p(r,z,t)=h(r,t)-z\). The horizontal equation is \[u_t+(u\cdot\nabla_r)u+w u_z+\nabla_r h=0,\qquad w_z+\operatorname{div}_r u=0.\] This is the hydrostatic long-wave model, not the full free-surface Euler system.
reconstruction: The pressure sign, surface-pressure condition and scaling assumptions are made explicit. The bracket marking terms to neglect in the notebook does not include every vertical-acceleration term; \(w_t\) must also be negligible for the displayed reduction.
fate: The long-wave system is the starting point, credited to Benney, in \citet[Sec.~1, Eqs.~(1)--(4)]{zakharov1980benney} and \citet[Sec.~1]{zakharov1981benney}. Their introduction identifies the previously studied model, while their new claims concern its structure.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The formal reduction is established under the stated approximation. Its validity over a specified error scale and time interval requires a separate asymptotic justification.

title: The height equation is integrated mass conservation
notes: The third displayed equation is \(h_t+\operatorname{div}\int_0^h u\,dz=0\); the notes say that the one-dimensional system had been studied by Manin and others.
statement: If \(h>0\) and \(u,w,h\) are smooth, impose \(w(r,0,t)=0\) and the kinematic free-surface condition \(h_t+u(r,h,t)\cdot\nabla_r h=w(r,h,t)\). Integrating incompressibility and differentiating the moving upper limit yields \[h_t+\operatorname{div}_r\int_0^{h(r,t)}u(r,z,t)\,dz=0.\] Together with the horizontal equation and incompressibility, this is the displayed Benney system.
reconstruction: The bed and free-surface boundary conditions are required to derive the equation; they are not all written in the fragment.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{zakharov1980benney} and \citet[Eqs.~(1)--(4)]{zakharov1981benney} explicitly start from this pre-existing long-wave system.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An exact mass balance within the smooth hydrostatic model. It does not require any assertion of complete integrability.

title: Additional branches generate conservation laws beyond the usual moment hierarchy
notes: Zakharov announces \ru{счетное число законов сохранения (гораздо больше, чем было)}: a countable collection, substantially more than previously known. No densities are written.
statement: A precise finite-layer reconstruction is \(\rho_{a,t}+(\rho_a u_a)_x=0\), \(u_{a,t}+u_a u_{a,x}+h_x=0\), \(h=\sum_{a=1}^{N}\rho_a\), with smooth fields and distinct velocities on the region considered. Set \[R(p)=p+\sum_{a=1}^{N}\frac{\rho_a}{p-u_a}.\] Each formal inverse branch \(R(p)=\lambda\) satisfies \(p_t+\partial_x(p^2/2+h)=0\). Expansion of the branch at infinity yields the standard moment densities; the additional branches approaching the \(u_a\) give further conservation-law sequences. Their integrals are conserved for periodic fields or suitable decay.
reconstruction: The finite-layer system and formal expansions are reconstructed from the identified papers. The continuum-label limit needs additional analytic or formal-series hypotheses and, for the displayed non-polynomial formulas in the paper, a specified principal-value prescription. The notebook does not state a completeness theorem for these integrals.
fate: \citet[Sec.~4, Eqs.~(48)--(52)]{zakharov1980benney}, received 17 December 1979 and published in 1980, develops the announcement; \citet[Sec.~4, Eqs.~(35)--(39)]{zakharov1981benney} displays the extra branches and involution argument. The latter explicitly says that completeness, needed for full integrability, is not proved.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The formal conservation hierarchies are established for the stated reductions. They do not by themselves prove global solvability or complete integrability of every smooth Benney solution.

title: Lagrangian layers give a simpler one-dimensional Hamiltonian bracket
notes: Zakharov announces \ru{более простая гамильтонова структура}, and says that the idea is a reinterpretation of the equation.
statement: Use a material vertical label \(a\) and a smooth monotone height coordinate \(z=z(x,a,t)\) with \(\rho=z_a>0\). In a fixed label interval, let \(h=\int\rho\,da\). The equations become \(\rho_t+\partial_x(\rho u)=0\), \(u_t+u u_x+h_x=0\). With periodic or decaying fields, \[E=\tfrac12\int\!\left(\int\rho u^2\,da+h^2\right)dx,\qquad \binom{\rho_t}{u_t}=-\begin{pmatrix}0&\partial_x\\\partial_x&0\end{pmatrix}\binom{\delta E/\delta\rho}{\delta E/\delta u},\] where the bracket includes \(\delta(a-b)\) in the label variable. Thus the bracket has constant coefficients in these variables.
reconstruction: The precise fields, energy, boundary conditions and bracket are absent from the notes. The coordinate change is valid only while the layers remain smooth and the vertical parametrization stays invertible.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2]{zakharov1980benney}, manuscript received December 1979, and \citet[p.~195, Eqs.~(11)--(12)]{zakharov1981benney} give this Hamiltonian formulation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established locally in these smooth variables. This simple bracket must not be confused with a proof of existence of global smooth solutions.

One definite potential-flow version has horizontal \(r\in\mathbb R^2\), layer density \(ho(r,a,t)>0\), potential \(\phi(r,a,t)\), \(u=

title: Gelfand interprets the system as collective differential equations
notes: Gelfand describes particles that do not interact directly, but jointly produce a field (an electric field is mentioned) which acts on every particle; he proposes studying such collective equations after ordinary differential equations.
statement:
A precise schematic model is a kinetic transport equation \(\partial_t f+v\cdot
abla_xf+F[f]\cdot
abla_vf=0\), where the common field \(F[f]\) is determined by the distribution through a separately specified field equation. The Benney reinterpretation uses \(F[f]=-
abla_x\int f\,dv\); an electrostatic plasma uses a Poisson field instead. These are different closures of the same collective-dynamics idea.
reconstruction: The schematic equation and distinction between closures explain the analogy; no unique field equation or new well-posedness problem can be extracted from the intervention alone.
fate: The general collective-field concept predates the talk: \citet[Secs.~1--2]{vlasov1968vibrational} is the English version of the 1938 paper, as the publisher\textquotesingle s Russian reprint record explicitly confirms. The specific Benney closure is given in \citet[Eq.~(15)]{zakharov1981benney}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established interpretation, not a newly stated precise conjecture. The original Vlasov publisher record and table of contents were checked; its full proof was not needed for the displayed Benney identity.
